findings.description: The code is `[SerializeField] AudioSource chime;` left unassigned, and the panel shows a plain NullReferenceException that names only the method. In the Unity Editor, an unassigned serialized UnityEngine.Object field holds a 'fake null', so `chime.Play()` throws 'UnassignedReferenceException: The variable chime of BayDoor has not been assigned…', which names the field. The panel therefore does not show what students will see in Play mode.
findings.evidence: Unity cannot run here. In plain .NET with a UnityEngine stub, the call throws NullReferenceException at S19.BayDoor.OnTriggerEnter. The fake-null / UnassignedReferenceException behavior for serialized fields is documented Unity editor behavior: the same mechanism produces MissingComponentException, and the 'The variable X of Y has not been assigned' message is widely reported. The Unity Manual's inspecting-scripts page simplifies this to 'A NullReferenceException is thrown if a variable requiring Inspector initialization is not set', so I fixed the code side, which is correct under either reading. A private field that is not serialized is a real C# null in the editor and in builds, so the shown NRE text and the 'Consola, en ejecución' label stay accurate. Side effect: Unity also shows the compile warning CS0649 'Field 'BayDoor.chime' is never assigned to', which I confirmed with Roslyn.

findings.description: The built slide drops the digits of every C# float literal. The YAML says `float d = 10f;`, `* 0.5f *` and `2f * d`, but the .pptx shows `float d = f;`, `cam.fieldOfView * 0.f * Mathf.Deg2Rad;` and `float h = f * d * Mathf.Tan(half);`. That code does not compile and contradicts the output panel. Cause: in the committed kit/highlight.py, `_TOKEN_RE` has `num = \b\d+\.?\d*\b`, which cannot match a number followed by a letter, and `op = [^\sA-Za-z_0-9]` excludes digits. So `finditer` skips the digits without any warning. Hex `0x1F` and exponent `1e5` literals are hit the same way. This affects every deck with suffixed literals; Unity alone has 28 such lines, e.g. w04 `90f`.
findings.evidence: I read the shape text out of the built w05.es.pptx and w05.en.pptx with python-pptx and compared it line by line with the YAML source. Only these 3 lines of slide 8 differ, in both decks. I loaded `git show HEAD:ppts/kit/highlight.py` on its own and called highlight(): 'float d = 10f;' gives 'float d = f;', '0.5f' gives '0.f', '2f' gives 'f', '1e5' gives 'e5', '0x1F' gives 'x1F'. The contact-sheet preview shows the same broken lines.
findings.fix_summary: Not fixed: the defect is in ppts/kit/highlight.py, which I may not edit. Proposed fix: change the num group of _TOKEN_RE (and of the new _TOKEN_RE_C) to `\b0[xX][0-9A-Fa-f]+\b|\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?[fFdDmMuUlL]*\b`, and add a final catch-all `(?P<other>.)` so the tokenizer can never drop a character silently. The YAML code is correct and was left as written. A YAML workaround (`10`, `/ 2`, `2 * d`) would hide a bug that affects many other decks.

findings.description: The audio slides model Max Distance as the end of a straight fade. Step 04 says the default 500 'never fades indoors'. The answer slide says that with Spatial Blend 1 and Max 500 a 20 m room 'uses four percent of the curve, so it still sounds nearly flat'. Both are false for Unity's default Volume Rolloff, Logarithmic, which the deck's own table lists as the default: there the volume is Min/d no matter what Max is. With Min 1 the chime is at 50 percent at 2 m and 5 percent at 20 m, a steep fade. The 4 percent / nearly-flat argument, and the Min 1 / Max 20 recipe, are only right for Linear rolloff.
findings.evidence: Read the AudioSourceInspector.cs source at the 6000.3.7f1 tag (the course version per w01). Logarithmic rolloff is `LogarithmicValue(...) => minDistance / distance`, sampled from min/max to 1. Linear is `AnimationCurve.Linear(min/max, 1, 1, 0)`. Computed values: log at 20 m = 0.05; linear with Max 500 at 20 m = 0.962; linear with Max 20 at 20 m = 0.

findings.description: The risk note says that leaving Play On Awake checked makes the chime sound when the scene loads. Play On Awake plays the AudioSource's own clip field. DoorChime keeps its clip in its serialized `chime` field and plays it with PlayOneShot(chime). If RequireComponent adds the Audio Source, that source has no clip, and Play On Awake plays nothing. The risk is real only when the Audio Source also holds the clip, for example when the .wav was dragged onto the door as in step 02.
findings.evidence: Compiled DoorChime.cs unchanged (C# 9, net10) against minimal UnityEngine stubs: it compiles (only CS0649 on `chime`, which the Inspector assigns) and OnTriggerEnter fires PlayOneShot(chime) only for a collider with attachedRigidbody. The reading of Play On Awake follows the AudioSource.playOnAwake / AudioSource.clip semantics.
findings.fix_summary: ES: 'Si el Audio Source también trae el clip, Play On Awake marcado lo hace sonar en cuanto carga la escena, antes de que se mueva ninguna caja.' EN to match. The label stays Riesgo/Risk and keeps the single accent.

findings.description: Error 04 ("Compilar dentro de Assets" / "Building into the Assets folder") said the importer imports your own build, the project grows every time and the next build includes the previous one. Unity 6.3 never gets that far. It refuses any build path inside Assets (and also the project root) with an "Invalid build path" dialog.
findings.evidence: Fetched Unity's C# reference source at tag 6000.3.7f1 (Editor/Mono/BuildPlayerWindowBuildMethods.cs). PickBuildLocation calls IsBuildPathValid, and that rejects <project>/Assets, ProjectSettings, Library, Packages and UserSettings with the message "The 'Assets' directory is an internal work directory of Unity and projects should not be built inside it". The project root gets "The project root directory should not be used as a build output directory". The dialog title is "Invalid build path". The same source shows that a Windows build asks for a folder and names the exe Paths.MakeValidFileName(PlayerSettings.productName).exe, which confirms StoreRoom.exe and the Builds/Windows convention.
findings.fix_summary: Replaced the card text: es "Unity lo rechaza con el aviso Invalid build path, porque Assets es una carpeta interna de trabajo. La raíz del proyecto tampoco sirve. Usa Builds/Windows." and en "Unity refuses it with an Invalid build path dialog, because Assets is one of its internal work folders. The project root is refused too. Use Builds/Windows." This also removes the clash between "Build outside the project" and the Builds/Windows convention on slide 8.

findings.description: The answer trace for the quiz goes 'Habilita, segunda vez' (2) straight to 'Habilita, tercera vez' (3) with no disable between them. OnEnable cannot fire on an object that is already enabled, so that row sequence cannot happen. The quiz says the object is disabled and enabled twice, which means two Disable steps.
findings.evidence: I ran the quiz OnEnable source verbatim against a UnityEvent stub that appends without a duplicate check, as Unity's InvokableCallList does: enable 1 gives 1, disable gives 1, enable 2 gives 2, disable gives 2, enable 3 gives 3, and one grab printed 3 lines. The slide was missing the second disable row.
findings.fix_summary: Added the row ["Deshabilita otra vez", "2, sigue puesto", "0, el objeto está apagado"] / ["Disable again", "2, still attached", "0, object is off"] between the second and third enable.

findings.description: Error 04 is titled 'Suscrito dos veces' / 'Subscribed twice' and says the object was disabled and re-enabled once. That gives two listeners, but the text says the sound 'suena tres veces' / 'plays three times'.
findings.evidence: In the stub simulation, one load enable plus one disable/enable cycle leaves 2 listeners, so one grab runs the handler twice.
findings.fix_summary: 'tres veces' -> 'dos veces'; 'three times' -> 'twice'.

findings.description: The annotation 'public, un argumento' says the inspector ONLY lists public methods that take one argument of the event's type. That is false. The UnityEvent inspector also lists zero-argument public methods and static calls with one float, int, string, bool or Object parameter. The homework on slide 26 depends on exactly that, since inspector-only wiring of a sound uses AudioSource.Play(), which takes no arguments.
findings.evidence: Unity UnityEvent inspector semantics: Static calls take 0 or 1 argument of a basic type or Object, and Dynamic calls take the event's own argument type. The event-type parameter is only needed to receive the event data.
findings.fix_summary: es: 'Para recibir los datos del evento, el inspector pide un método público con un argumento de ese tipo.' en: 'To pass the event data along, the inspector needs a public method with one argument of the event's own type.' The label is unchanged.

findings.description: The lead says an interactor and an interactable 'nunca guardan una referencia el uno del otro' / 'never hold a reference to each other'. At runtime they do: interactables keep interactorsSelected and interactorsHovering, and interactors keep interactablesSelected and interactablesHovered. The point the slide wants to make is that they never find each other; the manager matches them.

findings.description: The 'Buscar quién llama' row says an inspector binding does not show up in a search, and the English says 'Not in a text search'. With Unity's default Force Text serialization, the .unity scene stores m_MethodName: Held, so a project-wide text search does find it. What is true is that it is not in the code.
findings.evidence: Default Asset Serialization Mode is Force Text, and persistent calls are serialized with m_TargetAssemblyTypeName and m_MethodName.

findings.fix_summary: 'colour' -> 'color'.

findings.description: 'Qué imprime el banco al cargar' shows four 'registrado ...' lines on entering Play mode. That only happens if BenchRegistry.OnEnable subscribes before the interactables' OnEnable registers them. XRI gives interactables an earlier execution order (k_Interactables = -98) than a user script (0), and even without that the order would be undefined. A real load could print nothing. The deck itself warns that load order shows up as bugs.
findings.evidence: XRI 3.5 docs (Context7): XRInteractionUpdateOrder.k_Interactables = -98 and XRInteractionManager is [DefaultExecutionOrder(-105)]. Unity's own InteractableRegisteredEventArgs sample says that components created before subscribing 'the initial register callback will not be logged'. In my stub run, subscribing after registration printed nothing, and subscribing first printed exactly the slide's four lines (the format string is correct).
findings.fix_summary: Not fixed: I cannot confirm this without running Unity, and the fix changes the code. Options for the instructor: add [DefaultExecutionOrder(-106)] to BenchRegistry, or iterate manager.GetRegisteredInteractables in OnEnable, or relabel the output as what prints when objects are toggled after load.

findings.description: The panel note says that without the phase check the dial turns 'al doble' / 'twice as fast'. XRInteractionManager calls ProcessInteractable in four phases: Fixed (once per fixed step), Dynamic, Late and OnBeforeRender. An unchecked Rotate(spin*Time.deltaTime) therefore turns the dial about four times as fast, not two.
findings.evidence: Simulated 1 s at 72 fps with a 50 Hz fixed step (Time.deltaTime = fixedDeltaTime in the Fixed phase), calling ProcessInteractable per phase. With the slide 16 phase check: 90.0 deg. Without it: 358.2 deg (3.98x). XRGrabInteractable's own ProcessInteractable switches on all four phases.
findings.fix_summary: Changed to 'gira varias veces más rápido de lo que tecleaste' / 'turns several times as fast as the number you typed'.

findings.description: Error 03 states flatly that per-frame work in Update reads the previous frame's selection and lags by exactly one frame. XRInteractionManager has DefaultExecutionOrder -105 and updates selection in its Update. A MonoBehaviour at the default order (0) runs after it and sees the current frame's selection. The lag only happens when the script executes before the manager.
findings.evidence: Checked against the XRI source and docs (XRInteractionUpdateOrder.k_InteractionManager = -105, applied with [DefaultExecutionOrder] on XRInteractionManager). Not executable here; listed under unverifiable.
findings.fix_summary: Made the claim conditional: 'Corre fuera de las fases de interacción. Si se ejecuta antes que el manager, la carátula lee la selección del cuadro anterior...' and the matching English sentence.

findings.description: The Spanish brief says the motor refuses to start 'mientras la puerta no esté cerrada y el paro no esté liberado', which reads as refusing only when both conditions fail (a De Morgan error). The English brief is correct: 'unless the door is closed and the stop is clear'.
findings.evidence: Logic: refuse = NOT(closed AND clear) = (NOT closed) OR (NOT clear). The Spanish text gave (NOT closed) AND (NOT clear), so an open door with the stop released would start the motor.
findings.fix_summary: Changed to 'se niegue a arrancar a menos que la puerta esté cerrada y el paro liberado', matching the English.

findings.description: The rubric grades the interlock on 'Tres condiciones' / 'Three conditions', but the lab the homework asks students to finish names only two (door closed, stop released). findings.description: Error 03 says that frame timing is off by default in release builds, so 'el mismo código no reporta nada' / 'the same code reports nothing'. The deck's own code is a ProfilerRecorder (slide 13). According to the Unity manual, attaching a ProfilerRecorder turns the FrameTimingManager on automatically, including in release builds, without Frame Timing Stats. Only direct FrameTimingManager reads (GetLatestTimings) return nothing.
findings.evidence: Unity 6 manual, 'Enable frame timing statistics for release builds' (found through web search; docs.unity3d.com is blocked by the proxy): 'If you use ProfilerRecorder ... you don't need to enable the Frame Timing Stats property ... FrameTimingManager is enabled automatically including in release builds'.

Elsewhere the deck gives other numbers for the same bench. Slide 15 says the run averaged 8.1 ms with only 4 of 600 frames late. Slide 21 says the change took the main thread from 8.1 to 7.4 ms. Slide 14's worst frame is 21.4, not 14.2. The cover notes say all millisecond figures came from this bench, so a student cannot reconcile them.

findings.description: The panel shows adb forward printing '34999' and says adb reverse prints nothing. In adb, forward and reverse send their reply through the same path (handle_forward_request returns the resolved TCP port). Either both print the port or neither does, depending on the adb version. The adb man page documents printing only for tcp:0.
findings.evidence: No adb binary or headset is available here, and android.googlesource.com is blocked. This is based on reading the adb source from memory plus the man page found through search.
findings.fix_summary: Not changed. The instructor should run both commands once on the classroom PC and copy what they actually print.

verdicts.finding: 1. Highlighter drops the digits of C# float literals on slide 8 (10f, 0.5f, 2f)
verdicts.note: I reproduced it. The kit/highlight.py in the working tree is unchanged from HEAD, and highlight() still turns 'float d = 10f;' into 'float d = f;', '0.5f' into '0.f', '2f' into 'f', '1e5' into 'e5' and '0x1F' into 'x1F'. Only the 3 literal lines of slide 8 differ from the YAML; every other code line on slides 8, 15, 16 and 21 matches. check.sh reports CLEAN even so, because no check catches dropped characters. The fix belongs in ppts/kit/highlight.py: the num group of _TOKEN_RE and _TOKEN_RE_C needs suffix, exponent and hex support, plus a catch-all group. The YAML C# is idiomatic and correct, so I left it alone. Severity stays high: until the kit is fixed, both decks show code that does not compile.

verdicts.finding: 2. Audio rolloff: Max 500 'never fades' and the 4 percent claim are only true for Linear rolloff
verdicts.note: I checked AudioSourceInspector.cs (6000.3.7f1). Logarithmic draws as Logarithmic(min/max,...), and LogarithmicValue returns minDistance/distance. That gives 0.05 at 20 m with Min 1, a steep fade. Linear is AnimationCurve.Linear(min/max,1,1,0), which gives (500-20)/(500-1) = 0.962 at 20 m. Step 04 now sets Linear explicitly, so the method point (scoped to Linear) and the answer title ('the first is the next problem') hold together. Option B is still the only answer that explains equal loudness. The slide 13 table ('Where the fade stops', default Logarithmic) is right for both modes. The longer step 04 text builds without overflow.

verdicts.finding: 3. Stat note: 12 m ramp vs 11.55 m visible height does not fit (it is not 'almost no margin')

The fix matches the lab, which asks students to record the field of view they needed (2*atan(0.6) = 61.9 deg). The ES wording 'no cabe por 45 centímetros' and the EN '45 centimeters too long' are accurate and build cleanly.

new_findings.description: Pitfall 04 says two cameras with the same Priority make 'the image flicker between them' / 'la imagen parpadea entre ellas'. URP orders cameras deterministically every frame, so the symptom is a steady wrong camera on top, not flicker. A student looking for flicker would misdiagnose the problem.
new_findings.evidence: URP UniversalRenderPipelineCore.cs (Graphics 6000.3/staging) sorts with cameraComparison = (int)c1.depth - (int)c2.depth through List.Sort/Array.Sort, which returns the same order for the same input each frame (for 2 cameras it is an insertion sort, so nothing is swapped on a tie). The Priority tooltip in UniversalRenderPipelineCameraUI.Rendering.Skin.cs reads 'A camera with a higher priority is drawn on top'.
new_findings.fix_summary: ES: 'Las dos dibujan, en un orden que nadie prometió, y la que queda encima puede no ser la que querías.' EN: 'Both render, in an order nobody promised, and the one left on top may not be the one you meant.' The rest of the card (raise one Priority; Depth in the built-in pipeline) is unchanged. The build is CLEAN.

new_findings.description: Step 05 says that closing the Sprite Editor without Apply throws the slicing away ('Cerrarla sin eso tira el corte'). That is not what happens: on close the Sprite Editor asks whether to apply or revert the unapplied changes.

The window moved to the com.unity.2d.sprite package later. That package's source is not reachable from here, but the dialog is the documented behavior of the same window.
new_findings.fix_summary: ES: 'La barra de arriba de la ventana. Mientras no apliques, el corte no se guarda.' EN: 'The bar at the top of the window. Until you apply, the slicing is not saved.' The new text is true whether or not the dialog appears. The build is CLEAN.

findings.description: The comment vs note table had the shortcuts swapped. It gave Shift+F2 for a threaded comment and 'Ctrl+Shift+F2, to confirm' for a note. In Microsoft 365, Shift+F2 inserts or edits a note and Ctrl+Shift+F2 inserts a threaded comment or replies to one.

The same wrong mapping is in procedures.en.md and procedures.es.md 1.2.5 'Shortcut', which this audit did not edit.

findings.description: The row said to leave 'Format cells' on when 'Column widths may change'. Column width is controlled by the separate 'Format columns' permission. 'Format cells' covers only the Format Cells and Conditional Formatting dialogs.
findings.evidence: Microsoft's Protect Sheet permission definitions: Format cells covers the Format Cells and Conditional Formatting dialogs; Format columns covers column formatting commands including changing column width. The product-read glossary (procedures.es.md, source key IMG) gives 'Format columns' as 'Aplicar formato a columnas', and the lowercase 'Format cells' permission as 'Aplicar formato a celdas', not 'Formato de celdas'.

findings.description: Error 03 claimed that TRUE over an unsorted table 'returns the row above the key'. It does not. Excel's binary search on unsorted data returns an unpredictable row and sometimes #N/A. Microsoft's documentation only says it 'might not return the correct value'.
findings.evidence: I shuffled the 23-row Fees table from ex20-fees.csv and ran a standard approximate binary search: 21 of 23 keys that are present came back wrong. One was #N/A (Anthropology). Others got unrelated rows, e.g. Business returned 25 instead of 86. None of these is 'the row above the key'.
findings.fix_summary: Now reads 'VERDADERO sobre una tabla sin ordenar puede devolver la fila de otra clave' / 'TRUE over an unsorted table can return another key's row'.

findings.description: Both places said an unsorted table returns 'the neighbour's fee/value'. The neighbour's value is what you get when a key is MISSING from a SORTED table. That is the Fees case (Fees is alphabetical) and the quiz answer. On an unsorted table the result is arbitrary.
findings.evidence: Simulation on ex20-fees.csv, which is sorted alphabetically (checked True): 'Economics' returns 58, the fee of East Asian Language and Culture, the program just before it; 'Accounting' returns #N/A. On the shuffled table, results are arbitrary (see the Error 03 finding).
findings.fix_summary: Annotation now says a program that is missing brings back the neighbour's fee ('un programa que no está trae la cuota del vecino' / 'a program that is missing returns a neighbor's fee'). Takeaway now says 'el valor de otra fila' / 'another row's value'.

findings.description: The step 'Camina a la derecha tantas columnas como diga Indicador_columnas / It walks right by Col_index_num columns' is off by one. Col_index_num counts the key column as 1, so 2 means one step right. As written it contradicts the counting rule on slides 7 and 10.

findings.description: The slide said '*8 termina en 8'. In an Advanced Filter, a text criterion without = is matched as 'begins with', so *8 behaves like *8* and returns any code that contains an 8. Microsoft documents this: typing 'Dav' finds Davolio, David and Davis. The lab's own text says the same ('E and E* do the same thing'). To get 'ends in 8' you write ="=*8".
findings.evidence: Python wildcard simulation on the 27 codes. Begins-with semantics: *8 gives 7 codes (SU-AHI98, ED-SAC88, DI-LER98, MI-RLB28, ED-ASD85, ED-OAS81, AU-FHW89). Whole-cell semantics (="=*8") gives the 4 that end in 8, which is the answer the lab expects. E*, ?E* and *A* give the same result under both semantics (7, 4 and 13 codes). Excel itself could not be run here.
findings.fix_summary: Changed the source line to ="=*8" and the annotation to '="=*8" termina en 8. Sin el igual, *8 acepta cualquier 8.' Shortened the first annotation to keep the slide within its limits, and added speaker notes explaining the change.

findings.description: The Riesgo annotation said that NPER giving a negative number or #¡NUM! means Pago and Va have the same sign. With a positive rate, same signs always give a negative number, never #NUM!. #NUM! appears when the signs are opposite and the payment is at or below the per-period interest.
findings.evidence: LibreOffice NPER (same formula as Excel): NPER(0.154/12,12169.23,250000) = -18.35; NPER(0.154/12,-12169.23,-250000) = -18.35; NPER(0.154/12,-3000,250000) = Err:503 (#NUM!), where 3000 is below the 3,208 interest per period; NPER(0.01,-2500,250000) = #NUM!. Algebra: n = ln(pmt/(pmt+pv*r))/ln(1+r), and the log argument is negative only when the payment does not cover pv*r.
findings.fix_summary: Changed to: 'Si NPER da negativo, Pago y Va traen el mismo signo. Si da #¡NUM!, el pago no cubre ni el interés.'

The unsigned demo on slide 9 is well-defined and prints 4294967295, which matches the slide.

findings.description: The row 'Valor o referencia / f(int) y f(int&)' says 'Compila: No, da C2668' (en 'No, C2668'). That is false. The two overloads declare and compile together. C2668 (ambiguous call) only appears when f is called with an lvalue int, and f(5) resolves to f(int) without any problem.
findings.evidence: g++ 13 and clang++ with -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra: f(int){} + f(int&){} + f(5) compiles and prints 'f(int)'. Adding int x=5; f(x); gives 'call of overloaded f(int&) is ambiguous' (clang: 'call to f is ambiguous'). That is the MSVC C2668 situation.
findings.fix_summary: The cell now reads 'Sí, pero f(x) da C2668' / 'Yes, but f(x) is C2668'.

findings.fix_summary: Changed to 'Va en el prototipo si existe, nunca en ambos, o el compilador lo rechaza' / 'It goes in the prototype if there is one, never in both, ...'.

findings.description: The lede said that in C++ a condition "vale 1 o 0". In C++ (unlike C), a relational or logical expression has type bool and value true/false. It only prints as 1/0 and converts to int 1/0. The lede also contradicted the next table, whose "Da" column says true/false. Same in en ("it is worth 1 or 0").
findings.evidence: g++ -std=c++20: typeid(7==7).name() is "b" (bool). With boolalpha it prints true; without it, cout prints 1.
findings.fix_summary: es: "En C++ es un bool, se imprime como 1 o 0 y se puede guardar." en: "A condition is an expression that evaluates to true or false. In C++ it is a bool, prints as 1 or 0, and can be stored." (This also removes the "worth true or false" calque.)

findings.description: Error 01 said an assignment in an if "se cumple siempre y no hay advertencia", and takeaway 1 said "se cumple siempre". This is false when the assigned value is 0 (`if (x = 0)` never fires), and the deck's own trace verdict says so correctly ("verdadera con cualquier valor distinto de cero"). "No hay advertencia" is true only for the build output at MSVC's default /W3 (C4706 is a level-4 warning). g++ -Wall and clang warn by default, and the VS IntelliSense linter may underline it. Same claims in en.
findings.evidence: g++ -Wall: "suggest parentheses around assignment used as truth value [-Wparentheses]". clang++: "using the result of an assignment as a condition without parentheses". The course compiler is MSVC in Visual Studio 2026 (w00/w01, C2248 in w06).
findings.fix_summary: es pitfall: "Asigna en lugar de comparar, se cumple con cualquier valor distinto de cero y compila sin advertencia". es takeaway: "...se cumple con cualquier valor distinto de cero y modifica la variable". en pitfall: "It assigns rather than compares, fires on any nonzero value, and compiles with no warning". en takeaway: "...fires on any nonzero value, and modifies the variable". Rendered and checked: no overflow.

findings.description: Looks suspicious but is not a defect. `std::cout << (x = 6) << " " << x` modifies and reads x in one expression. GCC 13 warns "operation on 'x' may be undefined [-Wsequence-point]" even in C++20. Since C++17 (P0145), the operands of << are sequenced left to right, so "6 6" is guaranteed under the course's /std:c++20. Under C++14 (MSVC's default when the standard is not set) it would be undefined behavior.
findings.evidence: g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra prints "6 6" plus 2 -Wsequence-point warnings (a GCC false positive). clang++ -std=c++20 prints "6 6" with no warning. Same code in en (equals.cpp).
findings.fix_summary: No change: the output is correct for C++20, which w00/w01 have students set. The instructor could mention that it relies on C++17 ordering.

findings.description: Not a defect, noted for completeness. The switch fallthrough example compiles with -Wimplicit-fallthrough warnings under GCC -Wextra. The slide does not deny any warning, and the output is correct.
findings.evidence: g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra with opcion=2 prints "dos\ntres" and warns twice that a statement may fall through. The en version prints "two\nthree". Both match the output panels.
findings.fix_summary: No change needed.

findings.description: Error 02 'Punto y coma después del for' / 'A semicolon after the for' sits under the title 'Cuatro maneras de escribir un ciclo infinito', but a stray semicolon after a for does not loop forever. The for runs its empty body to completion and the block below runs once, which is exactly what the card's own desc says. The infinite case is a semicolon after a while, because then the step inside the block never runs.
findings.evidence: g++ 13 -std=c++20: `for (i = 0; i < 3; i++); { cout << "x" << i; }` prints 'x3' and terminates. `while (i < 3); { i++; }` was still running when `timeout 2` killed it (exit 124). clang -Wempty-body flags both.

findings.description: The title says only dia_id got its own index because curso_id is the left column. findings.evidence: I built curso/aula/dia plus horario(curso_id, aula_id, dia_id, hora, PK of all four, three FKs) in MariaDB. Only a variant with no FK on aula_id gives 'only dia_id'. MySQL names the implicit FK index after the column the same way.
findings.fix_summary: Output panel now shows the real body lines: the PK with backticks, wrapped after a comma like slide 17, then KEY `aula_id` and KEY `dia_id`. Title es: 'aula_id y dia_id recibieron índice propio; curso_id ya es la columna izquierda'; en: 'aula_id and dia_id got their own index; curso_id is already the left column'.

findings.description: The note says 'La tabla ciudad se crea primero, con estado_id NOT NULL'. ciudad cannot be created first: its FK points to estado, which does not exist yet. The script works only in the order estado, then ciudad, then the ALTER, so ciudad must exist before the ALTER, not before estado. Same in en ('created first').
findings.evidence: In MariaDB, creating ciudad with its FK before estado failed with errno 150 (MySQL 8+: ERROR 1824 Failed to open the referenced table). The 'after' ALTER with no ciudad table also failed. The order estado (capital_id NULL), ciudad (FK to estado), ALTER worked, and inserting estado with NULL, then ciudad, then the UPDATE worked.
findings.fix_summary: es: 'La tabla ciudad se crea antes del ALTER, con estado_id NOT NULL.' en: 'The ciudad table is created before the ALTER, with estado_id NOT NULL.' The rest of the note is unchanged; the NULL is still what breaks the cycle for inserts, which I verified.

Bytes 8 to 11 '00 01 62 4e' = 90702 = the FIL_PAGE_SRV_VERSION stamp for 9.7.2, so the dump is consistent with a real file.
findings.fix_summary: Left as is (course-wide convention).

unverifiable: MySQL 9.7.2 could not be run here (MariaDB 10.11 only). Slide 13's datadir, the INNODB_TABLESPACES space IDs 417 to 419 and the FILE_SIZE values (MariaDB names the view INNODB_SYS_TABLESPACES) were checked only for plausibility: 8/8/7 pages of 16 KB, consistent with the secondary indexes each table has.
@@explain_format = TREE on 9.7.2: dev.mysql.com is blocked by the proxy. A web-search hit (rails issue #55958) says 9.5.0 changed the default to TREE.
EXPLAIN tree details on slide 18 (cost=1.05/0.7/0.35, rows=1, covering index scan on i using fk_ins_materia) depend on the author's data and statistics; MariaDB picks a different join order.
@@log_bin = 1: MySQL 8+ default is ON (MariaDB returned 0, a dialect difference).
The fifteen rows and the 6,963-byte dump come from week 17's measurements and were not re-measured.
That v_alumno_activo returns 'cuatro columnas' (its definition is never shown; alumno has 4 columns per w02).
Whether a non-admin Windows user can list the MySQL data directory for the lab's last step.

findings.description: Both INSERTs give 4 values to insc_desnorm, but slide 7 defines that table with 5 columns (calificacion is the fifth). The panel says both rows go in with no error and no warning.
findings.evidence: Ran slide 7 verbatim, then slide 17 verbatim in MariaDB 10.11 (strict mode). Both statements fail with ERROR 1136 (21S01): Column count doesn't match value count at row 1, and SELECT * returns an empty set. MySQL 8/9 gives the same 1136. With the fix, both rows go in, SHOW WARNINGS is empty, and the table shows Ana Lopez / Ana Lpez for alumno 1.
findings.fix_summary: Added NULL as the fifth value (no grade yet) to both VALUES lists in es and en. The longest line is 52 chars and the code card stays at 20.25 pt.

findings.description: Absolute claims: 'Ninguna función encima de la columna puede apoyarse en un índice' and 'Una función encima de una columna no puede usar índice'. These are false for the stated MySQL 9.7.2, which has functional key parts (8.0.13+) and indexed generated columns. They also contradict week 15, whose index table lists 'Funcional / WHERE con función / ((DATE(fecha_alta)))'. Pitfall 02 also said the patch 'deja la tabla sin índice', but the table keeps its PRIMARY KEY.
findings.evidence: EXPLAIN in MariaDB: after CREATE INDEX ix_prod ON pedido_no1fn(producto), the FIND_IN_SET(..REPLACE(producto..)) query is type=ALL with possible_keys NULL, while WHERE producto='camisa' uses ix_prod (type=ref). So the column's own index is lost, not every index. Read w15.es.yaml line 244.
findings.fix_summary: Changed to 'su índice' / 'its index' (slide 12) and 'el índice de esa columna' / 'that column's index' (slide 19). Pitfall 02 now says 'deja esa búsqueda sin índice' / 'leaves that search without an index'.

findings.description: 'Vuelve en la semana 9 al ordenar el grupo' / 'comes back in week 9 sorting a group': week 9 never revisits the rule that a function on a column loses the index.
findings.evidence: Searched w09.es/en for índice, función, CAST, index and function. The grupo slide ('Uno, diez, cien, dos, nueve') shows text sorting with no function and no index discussion. The only index in w09 is ix_grupo in a covering-scan EXPLAIN for LIMIT. Week 15 has both the functional index (line 244) and the leading-wildcard slide (line 383).
findings.fix_summary: Changed to 'Vuelve en la semana 15, con el índice funcional y el comodín inicial' / 'It comes back in week 15, with the functional index and the leading wildcard'.

findings.description: 'La unicidad no es parte de la primera forma normal, y el servidor lo demuestra' depends on the definition. It holds for the Elmasri/Navathe and Silberschatz definition (atomic domains only). Under C. J. Date's definition, 1NF includes 'no duplicate rows'. And MySQL accepting a keyless table shows only that MySQL does not enforce a key; it proves nothing about 1NF.
findings.evidence: In MariaDB the keyless CREATE and the SHOW CREATE with no PRIMARY KEY line behave as on the slide. MariaDB has no sql_require_primary_key (ERROR 1193). The ERROR 3750 (HY000) text matches MySQL's ER_TABLE_WITHOUT_PK (8.0.13+), truncated with '...'.
findings.fix_summary: Not changed: defensible under the mainstream textbook definition. Flagged so the instructor can soften 'lo demuestra' if wanted.

unverifiable: Slide 8: sql_require_primary_key and ERROR 3750 cannot run on MariaDB 10.11 (ERROR 1193 Unknown system variable). The message text was checked against MySQL's ER_TABLE_WITHOUT_PK from memory. On MySQL 8.0.18+, setting this session variable may need SYSTEM_VARIABLES_ADMIN or SESSION_VARIABLES_ADMIN, which root has.
Slide 13: the key name 'pedido_1fn.PRIMARY' is MySQL 8.0.19+ format. MariaDB prints 'PRIMARY'; error number and SQLSTATE 1062 (23000) match.
Slide 18: ERROR 3105 (HY000) 'The value specified for generated column ... is not allowed.' is MySQL-only. MariaDB returns 1906 '... has been ignored'. The MySQL text was checked from memory.
Slide 15: the DISTINCT row order (Edificio C before Edificio A) depends on scan order with no ORDER BY. It matches with minimal scaffolding of 2 employees inserted in id order.
MySQL 9.7.2 itself was not available; everything ran on MariaDB 10.11 in strict mode.

findings.description: Error 04 says hand-indexing the foreign key 'era tarea del programador en 2010, no hoy'. That is false for MySQL. InnoDB has created the child-side index automatically since MySQL 4.1.2 (2004), so the habit comes from other engines, not from 2010-era MySQL.
findings.evidence: MySQL 5.0/5.1 manual, FOREIGN KEY constraints: 'Such an index is created on the referencing table automatically if it does not exist. (This is in contrast to some older versions...)'. MySQL 5.1 shipped in 2008. Running the slide 9 CREATE TABLE confirms the server creates the index (KEY alumno_id).
findings.fix_summary: Changed it to 'La regla heredada de buenas prácticas viene de motores que no lo crean solos.'

findings.description: Same false date claim in English: 'was the programmer's job in 2010, not today'.
findings.evidence: Same evidence as the Spanish deck. InnoDB has created the foreign key index automatically since MySQL 4.1.2.
findings.fix_summary: Changed it to 'The inherited best-practice rule comes from engines that do not create it for you.'

findings.description: The lab constraint 'El script corre dos veces seguidas sin editarlo' and the rubric line 'Corre desde vacío, dos veces seguidas' make the script idempotent. That needs DROP TABLE/DATABASE IF EXISTS or CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS. DROP is first taught in week 7 and IF EXISTS in week 13, so a week-6 student cannot meet this requirement.
findings.evidence: A grep of es/w01 to w06 finds no DROP, IF EXISTS or IF NOT EXISTS. DROP first appears in w07 (agenda line 32 and the DDL table) and IF EXISTS in w13. Running CREATE TABLE twice without DROP fails with 'Table already exists'.
findings.fix_summary: The lab constraint now reads 'El script corre completo sobre una base vacía, sin editarlo. El orden de creación es parte de la entrega.' The rubric now reads 'Corre desde vacío, completo y sin editarlo'.

findings.description: Same requirement in English: 'runs twice in a row without editing' and 'Runs from empty, twice in a row'. It needs DROP/IF EXISTS, which is taught after week 6.
findings.evidence: Same grep as the Spanish deck: no DROP or IF EXISTS in weeks 1 to 6.
findings.fix_summary: The lab now reads 'The script runs start to finish on an empty database, without editing.' The rubric now reads 'Runs from empty, complete and unedited'.

Whether MySQL 9.7.2 exists as the stated engine version.

MySQL also accepts 'YYYYMMDD' and other delimiters such as '2026/03/12' (deprecated with a warning since 8.0.29, but still accepted). What the server rejects is day-first order.

findings.description: The title 'Dos maneras de vaciar una tabla y dos maneras de negarse' / 'Two ways to empty a table...' does not match the code. Only the TRUNCATE empties a table. The DELETE has WHERE matricula = '2001' and targets one row.

findings.fix_summary: New titles: 'Dos maneras de borrar y dos maneras de negarse' / 'Two ways to delete and two ways to refuse'.

findings.description: The ERROR 1451 text stops at 'a foreign key constraint fails' with no mark that the rest was cut. The real message continues with (`db`.`inscripciones`, CONSTRAINT `inscripciones_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`matricula`) REFERENCES `alumnos` (`matricula`)). The 1701 message on the same panel keeps its parenthetical, so the cut reads as the complete output.
findings.evidence: MariaDB: ERROR 1451 (23000): Cannot delete or update a parent row: a foreign key constraint fails (`...`.`inscripciones`, CONSTRAINT `inscripciones_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`matricula`) REFERENCES `alumnos` (`matricula`)). TRUNCATE gave ERROR 1701 (42000) as on the slide. MariaDB appends the FOREIGN KEY clause to 1701 as well (dialect difference).
findings.fix_summary: Marked the cut: 'key constraint fails (...)'. w08 s(padre_con_hijos) has the same unmarked cut; that is another deck and is not touched.

findings.description: The panel says LOCK TABLE 'llega completo en la semana 16' / 'arrives in full in week 16'. w16 covers row locks (FOR UPDATE, SKIP LOCKED, deadlocks) and mentions LOCK TABLES only once, in a pitfall ('LOCK TABLES también [confirma]'). It is not covered in full.
findings.evidence: grep -i lock es/w16.es.yaml: the only LOCK TABLES hit is line 456. In MariaDB, LOCK TABLE (singular) is accepted, which matches the slide's claim.
findings.fix_summary: Removed 'completo' / 'in full': 'llega en la semana 16' / 'arrives in week 16'.

findings.description: The DECIMAL(4,2) annotation reads 'Two digits, two decimals.' DECIMAL(4,2) has four digits. The Spanish says 'Dos enteros y dos decimales', which is right.
findings.evidence: MySQL DECIMAL(M,D) semantics: M=4 total digits, D=2 after the point. The 9999.9 insert gives ERROR 1264, confirmed in MariaDB.
findings.fix_summary: 'Two integer digits, two decimals.'

findings.description: The slide is titled 'Las mismas tablas' and labelled 'El guion de la semana 6, con tipos'. The w06 instructor script uses other tables (departamento, profesor, alumno with alumno_id INT, inscripcion, materia), not alumnos/inscripciones with matricula. The DDL shown here also has no FOREIGN KEY, yet slide 19's ERROR 1701 relies on inscripciones_ibfk_1.
findings.evidence: Read es/w06.es.yaml slides 6 to 16. Running slide 10's DDL alone gives no FK; I had to add one as scaffolding to reproduce slide 19.
findings.fix_summary: Not fixed. Adding an FK line overflows the card, and the inline 'REFERENCES' form behaves differently across MySQL versions. Flagged for the instructor.

findings.description: Agenda card 3 and the block 3 lede promise CREATE, ALTER, DROP and TRUNCATE. DROP is never shown or explained anywhere in the deck. ALTER appears only as a commented-out line (slide 8) and in the ENUM steps.

findings.fix_summary: Not fixed: covering DROP would need new content. Reported for the instructor.

findings.description: 'ahorra memoria' / 'saves memory' is measured with DATA_LENGTH, which is on-disk table size, not RAM. Defensible, because InnoDB pages also take buffer-pool space and 'memoria' is colloquial for storage in Spanish, but 'space' would be more precise in English.
findings.evidence: The information_schema.TABLES DATA_LENGTH definition. My MariaDB reproduction with CHAR(50) vs VARCHAR(50) gave 8929280 vs 3686400 bytes.
findings.fix_summary: Left as written; looks suspicious but is defensible.

findings.description: The DECIMAL annotation says 'Ese mismo promedio en FLOAT sale 8.700000127156576', but the slide shows no average. FLOAT(8.7) alone is 8.699999809265137, so a reader may think the number is wrong.
findings.evidence: Brute-forced FLOAT32 averages. AVG of three FLOAT grades averaging 8.7 (e.g. 7.0, 9.1, 10.0) gives exactly 8.700000127156576. MariaDB returned AVG(c)=8.700000127156576 for FLOAT and 8.700000 for DECIMAL(4,2).
findings.fix_summary: Number verified as correct; the unstated referent is left to the author.

findings.description: 'AUTO_INCREMENT: sigue en 4 / vuelve a 1' refers to a 3-row demo that is never shown. Slide 17's t_prueba has 6 rows, so a reader may expect 7.
findings.evidence: MariaDB, 3-row AUTO_INCREMENT table: next id after DELETE = 4, after TRUNCATE = 1. Matches the slide.
findings.fix_summary: Correct as a fact; not changed.

unverifiable: Exact MySQL 9.7.2 numbers on slide 13 (TABLE_ROWS 99651/95860, DATA_LENGTH 9977856/4734976): the column widths are not shown. MariaDB with CHAR(50)/VARCHAR(50) and 'AB  ' gives the same direction (ratio 2.4 vs the slide's 2.1); the slide's own 2.1 ratio is arithmetically right (9977856/4734976 = 2.107).

Exact MySQL wording of ERROR 1292 and 1701. MariaDB writes the column as `db`.`table`.`col` and appends the FOREIGN KEY clause to 1701. The slide's MySQL-style text matches the MySQL 8 message format I know, but I could not run MySQL 9.7.2 itself.

MySQL 9.7.2 as a release (used course-wide), and ALGORITHM=INSTANT for appending an ENUM member on MySQL 9.x. Verified on MariaDB (append INSTANT OK; mid-list insert refused with 1846, needs COPY) and consistent with the MySQL online DDL docs.
Slide 14 ENUM output depends on INSERTs that are not shown. With scaffolding rows (1 aprobado, 2 baja, 3 inscrito, 4 reprobado) MariaDB reproduces the panel exactly.

findings.description: The kit flagged this before I started: the annotation stack ran to 9.99 in. against a 9.70 in. limit (check_issues.txt).

findings.description: The atomicity panel showed 'ERROR 1644 (45000)', which is the SIGNAL error a trigger raises (SIGNAL is taught in w13), with no message, followed by narrated text ('conteo = 6 / la primera fila tampoco quedo') instead of real output. The objective on slide 3 says these are 'los mismos constraints de la semana 6', and w06 rejects an out-of-range grade with a CHECK, which gives ERROR 3819 (HY000).
findings.evidence: Ran the slide on MariaDB 10.11 with inscripciones.calificacion DECIMAL(4,2) CHECK (BETWEEN 0 AND 10), 6 rows already loaded. The multi-row INSERT failed on the CHECK (MariaDB: 4025/23000, its dialect for MySQL 3819/HY000), COUNT(*) stayed 6, and the MAT201 row was not inserted. Without a CHECK, DECIMAL(4,2) accepts 12.0, so a CHECK is required. w13 lines 252-275 show 1644 coming only from SIGNAL.
findings.fix_summary: Output is now the real MySQL text: "ERROR 3819 (HY000): Check constraint 'inscripciones_chk_1' is violated." then 'COUNT(*) / 6'.

findings.description: Same defect in English: SIGNAL error 1644 instead of the CHECK error, and the output panel of the English deck contained Spanish prose ('conteo = 6 / la primera fila tampoco quedo').

findings.fix_summary: Same real output as the Spanish deck (ERROR 3819 plus COUNT(*) 6), which reads the same in both languages.

findings.description: The decks say a ROLLBACK on MyISAM 'no hace nada y tampoco dice nada' (s19) and that 'el servidor no se queja' (s22). That is false: the ROLLBACK raises Warning 1196 'Some non-transactional changed tables couldn't be rolled back'. The s18 panel also showed narrated text ('la fila sigue ahi / el ROLLBACK no hizo nada', missing its accent) instead of output.
findings.evidence: Ran s18 on MariaDB 10.11: the ROLLBACK printed 'Warning (Code 1196): Some non-transactional changed tables couldn't be rolled back' and SELECT returned (1, uno). MySQL 8 and 9 push the same ER_WARNING_NOT_COMPLETE_ROLLBACK (1196) in ha_rollback_trans.
findings.fix_summary: s18 output is now the 1196 warning followed by 'id nombre / 1 uno'. s19 condition 3 now reads 'solo lo admite en la advertencia 1196, que nadie lee'. s22 now says 'el servidor no da ningún error'.

findings.description: Same as the Spanish deck: 'says nothing either' and 'the server does not complain' are false because of Warning 1196, and the s18 output in the English deck was Spanish prose.
findings.evidence: Same MariaDB run (Warning 1196, row 1 'uno' stays).
findings.fix_summary: Real output on s18. s19 now reads 'only admits it in warning 1196, which nobody reads'. s22 now reads 'the server raises no error'.

findings.description: The lab says one of the fifty enrollments points at 'un alumno dado de baja' and expects that run to bounce. In the course's own schema (w07 tipos.sql: estatus ENUM('inscrito','baja',...)) a withdrawn student is still a row in alumnos, so the foreign key accepts the enrollment, nothing bounces, and the 'La prueba' block cannot be done.
findings.evidence: FK checks existence only. On MariaDB, an INSERT referencing an existing alumnos row succeeds, and only a nonexistent matricula gives 1452 (same as s8).
findings.fix_summary: Changed to 'apuntando a una matrícula que no existe', which ties the lab to the s8 error.

findings.description: Same as the Spanish deck: 'a student who dropped out' still exists in alumnos, so the FK lets the row in and the expected bounce never happens.

findings.description: The statement said the ROLLBACK sentence is true 'tres veces de cada cuatro'. The four runs in block 3 undo twice (s15, s16) and fail twice (s17, s18), and the scenario count would be 1 of 4, so the ratio has no basis. Condition 1 also said ROLLBACK 'contesta que hizo cero cambios', but ROLLBACK always reports 0 rows affected, even when it did undo something, so that reply tells you nothing.
findings.evidence: Counted the s15 to s18 outcomes, confirmed by real runs (3->2, 6->5->4->5->6, HIS100 stays, MyISAM row stays). Ran 'START TRANSACTION; DELETE; ROLLBACK' and a bare 'DELETE; ROLLBACK': both ROLLBACKs printed 'Query OK, 0 rows affected'.
findings.fix_summary: Statement now says the sentence 'solo es cierta con tres condiciones que no menciona'. Condition 1 now ends 'el ROLLBACK contesta Query OK sin deshacer nada'. Same change in English.

findings.description: The sub-line lists 'Autocommit encendido' as a condition under which ROLLBACK undoes nothing. s15 shows @@autocommit = 1 and a ROLLBACK that does undo (3 -> 2), because START TRANSACTION opens a transaction. findings.fix_summary: es: 'Sin transacción abierta, un DDL de por medio, o una tabla que no es InnoDB'. en: 'No open transaction, ...'.

findings.description: The panel said IS NULL and IS NOT NULL 'son los únicos operadores que contestan verdadero o falso sobre un NULL'. That is false in MySQL: the NULL-safe operator <=> (and IS UNKNOWN / IS TRUE) also return true or false on a NULL.
findings.evidence: Ran in MariaDB, which behaves like MySQL here: SELECT NULL <=> NULL, NULL <=> 1, (NULL = NULL) IS UNKNOWN returned 1, 0, 1. Also, WHERE carrera <=> NULL returned 1 row. The lead's phrase 'cualquier comparación' was left alone as a standard simplification for =, <>, < and >.
findings.fix_summary: Removed 'únicos': '..., y contestan verdadero o falso sobre un NULL'.

findings.description: Same as in the Spanish deck: 'they are the only operators that answer true or false over a NULL' is false because MySQL also has <=> and IS UNKNOWN.
findings.evidence: Same run as for es: NULL <=> NULL returned 1 and carrera <=> NULL matched 1 row.
findings.fix_summary: Changed to 'and they answer true or false over a NULL'.

findings.description: 'La pregunta por la ausencia se escribe IS NULL, y es la única forma que contesta' is false, because carrera <=> NULL also answers.
findings.evidence: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM alumno WHERE carrera <=> NULL returned 1.
findings.fix_summary: Changed to '..., y esa sí contesta.'

findings.description: 'it is the only form that answers' is false, because <=> NULL also answers.
findings.evidence: Same run as for es.
findings.fix_summary: Changed to 'and that form does answer.'

findings.evidence: w03.es slide 'plan.sql' states that @@explain_format is TREE on MySQL 9.7.2, so the deck agrees with the course. MariaDB 10.11 printed the traditional grid (type=index, key=ix_grupo, Using index / type=ALL), which confirms the plan itself: a covering index scan for grupo and a table scan for nombre. The default explain_format on 9.7.2 could not be checked here.
findings.fix_summary: Not changed. If 9.7.2 actually defaults to TRADITIONAL, the source should read EXPLAIN FORMAT=TREE.

unverifiable: The alumno and inscripcion data is not in the repository. I built a 12-row alumno and 20-row inscripcion data set in MariaDB 10.11 (database audit_mysql#1_w09, dropped afterward) that satisfies every constraint on the slides, and every one of the 12 code_output panels (slides 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21) reproduced exactly. Pitfall Error 03 ('near '3' at line 1' for OFFSET without LIMIT): the query is not shown. The claim fits MySQL's grammar for SELECT ... FROM alumno OFFSET 3, because OFFSET is non-reserved and gets parsed as a table alias. MariaDB instead accepts OFFSET n ROWS and reports near ''. Cannot check against MySQL 9.7.2 here. LIMIT 2+1 -> near '+1' was confirmed.

Pitfall Error 04 (BINARY gives Warning 1287 'BINARY expr' is deprecated ... Please use CAST instead): MariaDB does not deprecate BINARY. The text matches MySQL 8.0.27+ behavior from memory and could not be run here.
The default @@explain_format on MySQL 9.7.2 (the w03 deck says TREE), which determines whether plain EXPLAIN prints the tree lines shown on slide 20.
Neither deck has speaker notes, and the same is true of all 34 MySQL decks, so there were no notes to audit.

findings.description: The Spanish formula used the Spain-style ';' argument separator. Mexican Excel (Español México) uses ',' as the list separator, so on the students' machines '=SI(D2>50000; "meta"; "abajo")' is rejected as a formula error. The keyed answer B ("abajo") then cannot happen, and distractor C ("Un error") becomes half true.
findings.evidence: Excel takes its argument separator from the Windows list separator, which is a comma for es-MX (exceltotal.com, 'Separador de argumentos de funciones en Excel'; Microsoft troubleshoot 'Errores de fórmula cuando el separador de lista no se ha ajustado'). The instructor's own Excel course for Mexican students uses commas (office/manejo-y-analisis-de-la-informacion es decks, e.g. =SI(B2>=70,"Aprobado","Reprobado")). LibreOffice Calc is not installed here, so I checked the logic in Python instead: 50000>50000 gives False, which is "abajo", and that matches key B. Other decks in this course still use ';' and need the same fix by their owners: w01.1.es s9 (the same formula), w06.es s10, w13.es s6 and w15.3.es s13 (BUSCARV).
findings.fix_summary: Changed the source line to =SI(D2>50000, "meta", "abajo"). The options are unchanged and B is still the only correct answer.

findings.description: The Error 03 card says an unclosed parenthesis is reported on the next line, with the problem above it. That stopped being true in Python 3.10. The course uses Python 3.12 or later (Colab, per w01.0), and there Python reports "'(' was never closed" on the line where the parenthesis opens.
findings.evidence: I removed a parenthesis from primer_programa.py in several places (lines 6, 9 and 11) and wrote small tests t1 to t5 and u1 to u6, then ran them on python3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13. Every case was reported on the opening line. With IPython/Colab compile flags (codeop PyCF_ALLOW_INCOMPLETE_INPUT), a missing paren on the last line gives 'incomplete input', still on that same line.
findings.fix_summary: Kept the title and the closing sentence and replaced the example with one that is true: a name misspelled where it is assigned gets reported where it is used. es: 'Si escribes mal un nombre al guardarlo, Python lo reclama donde lo usas. El problema está arriba.' en: 'Misspell a name where you store it and Python reports it where you use it. The problem is above.' I checked it by renaming promedio to promedo on line 6: the NameError is reported at line 10.

findings.description: Takeaway 2 says 'Por eso el error aparece cuando llega a esa línea, y no antes de arrancar' / 'the error shows up when it reaches that line, and not before it starts'. That is false for syntax errors, which CPython catches when it compiles the whole file before running any of it. It also contradicts slide 15 ('IndentationError, y no corre nada') and what students will see in the lab, where two of the three breakages are SyntaxErrors.
findings.evidence: parB.py (missing ')' on line 11, the last print) printed nothing before the SyntaxError. printLast.py (Print on line 11) printed lines 9 and 10 first, then raised NameError. Tested on python3.12.
findings.fix_summary: 'el error' became 'un NameError' (en: 'the error' became 'a NameError'), which is true and is the error type slide 15 introduces.

findings.description: Under 'Cinco reglas que Python aplica siempre', the Paréntesis row said 'SyntaxError, a veces una línea abajo' and the Comillas row said 'SyntaxError en esa línea o la siguiente'. In Python 3.10 and later, both errors are reported on the line that holds the unpaired bracket or quote, never the line below.
findings.evidence: On python3.12, removing a ')' gives "'(' was never closed" on the opening line (parA, parB, parC). Removing a '(' gives "unmatched ')'" on the same line (op1 to op4). Deleting the opening or closing quote gives 'unterminated string literal (detected at line 10)' on line 10 (q1, q2).
findings.fix_summary: Paréntesis: 'SyntaxError en la línea del que sobra' / 'SyntaxError on the stray one's line'. Comillas: 'SyntaxError en esa misma línea' / 'SyntaxError on that same line'. I kept both cells about as short as the originals so the row heights do not change.

findings.description: Error 03 said that if both for loops use i, the outer walk falls apart ('el recorrido se descompone'). That is how C behaves, not Python. A Python for takes its next value from its own iterator, so the outer loop still makes every pass. What goes wrong is any use of i after the inner loop, because it then holds the inner loop's last value.
findings.evidence: I ran pitfall3.py: an outer range(4) with an inner range(2), both using i. It made all 8 inner passes (4 x 2), and after each inner loop i was 1, so campanas[i] printed 'Meta' four times. The outer walk finished normally.
findings.fix_summary: desc -> 'Si los dos for usan i, el de adentro pisa al de afuera, y lo que use i después del interno lee la fila equivocada.'

findings.description: Same false claim in English: 'the walk falls apart'. In Python the outer loop is not disrupted. Only reads of i after the inner loop get the wrong value.
findings.evidence: Same run as the Spanish deck (pitfall3.py): 8 inner passes, outer loop complete, i equal to 1 after every inner loop.
findings.fix_summary: desc -> 'If both fors use i, the inner one overwrites the outer, and any use of i after the inner loop reads the wrong row.'

The evidence goes both ways. syllabus-com101.docx lists COM101 as 'Sem 1' in 10 of 12 programs, ejercicios.es.md says 'primer semestre', and the C# COM101 decks say 'Semestre 1'. But 'Semestre 2' may mean the 2026 academic period, and COM102 and COM103 also say 'Semestre 2'.
new_findings.evidence: git diff of es/w01.0.es.yaml and en/w01.0.en.yaml shows the change. Clave lines across the course: 1 'Semestre 1', 20 'Semestre 2'. I extracted the syllabus docx text: the 'Dónde se imparte' table has Sem 1 for 10 programs, Sem 2 for one and Sem 4 for one.
new_findings.fix_summary: Not changed in w01.1 because the meaning of 'Semestre N' is ambiguous. The instructor or orchestrator should decide once and apply it to all 21 COM101 Python decks, es and en, either reverting w01.0 or updating w01.1 and w02 to w17.

verdicts.finding: 16 pitfalls: an unclosed parenthesis is reported on the next line (Error 03)

Removing a ')' on lines 6, 9 or 11 of primer_programa.py, and on four extra multi-line cases (print/print, x = (1 + 2 / y = 3, a list missing its ']', a continued sum), always gives "'(' was never closed" on the opening line in 3.10, 3.12 and 3.13. The es and en replacements match, and the slide renders without overflow.

verdicts.finding: 20 takeaways: 'the error shows up when it reaches that line, and not before it starts'
verdicts.note: I confirmed it. With Print on line 11, lines 9 and 10 print before the NameError. A missing ')' or quote prints nothing, because the SyntaxError is raised before any line runs. 'un NameError' / 'a NameError' is true, and NameError is already introduced on slide 15. I also fixed slide 11, which made the same overclaim, so the takeaway and the comparison table now agree (see new findings).

verdicts.finding: 15 table: Paréntesis 'a veces una línea abajo' and Comillas 'en esa línea o la siguiente'
verdicts.note: I confirmed it on 3.12. A missing '(' gives "unmatched ')'" on the same line. A missing ')' gives "'(' was never closed" on the opening line. Deleting either quote gives 'unterminated string literal (detected at line N)' on line N. A mismatch like print("a"] is also reported on that same line. In Spanish, 'del que sobra' means the bracket left without a partner, and in English 'stray' is the usual word for an unmatched bracket. Both are accurate. The row heights still pass lint.

verdicts.finding: 15 table: Sangría 'Cuatro espacios marcan qué anida' presented as something Python enforces

findings.description: Step 1 says 'transacción abierta' / 'transaction open' right after connect(). Python's sqlite3, in its default legacy transaction control, opens no transaction on connect. It issues an implicit BEGIN only before the INSERT, which is step 2.

findings.description: The solutions say Git Bash reports 127 'because POSIX shells trim the status to eight bits'. The reason is wrong: trimming 0xE0434352 to eight bits gives 0x52 = 82. The deck itself only states the measured numbers, which are consistent.
findings.evidence: unchecked((int)0xE0434352) = -532462766, verified in C#. 0xE0434352 & 0xFF = 82.
findings.fix_summary: Must be fixed in the solutions files, which are outside my assignment.

The arithmetic is checked (0xE0434352 as int32 = -532462766, run in C#). The 127 matches Cygwin/MSYS2 mapping codes >= 0xC0000000 to 127 and matches the w13 deck's measurement. On Linux the same crash exits 134 (SIGABRT).

findings.description: The 'Si falla' annotation gave the wrong cause. It said VERDADERO on every row means a dollar sign is missing, or the active cell was wrong. A missing column $ paints only the first column. An extra row $ ($E$2) makes every row TRUE. A wrong active cell shifts the color by one row; it does not make every row TRUE.
findings.evidence: I built the rule in LibreOffice Calc (openpyxl, then soffice recalc) and filled it as relative copies over A2:F6, which is how CF evaluates it. =$E2="Atrasado" painted only rows 2 and 5 (the overdue rows). With the column $ missing (=E2=...), only column A was TRUE. With the extra row $ (=$E$2=...), all 30 cells were TRUE. With the active cell one row off (=$E{r-1}), the result came out as [False, True, False], so the color was shifted by one row.
findings.fix_summary: Now reads 'VERDADERO en todas las filas: sobra un signo de pesos, como en $E$2. Una fila de desfase: la celda activa no era la correcta.'

findings.fix_summary: Now reads 'TRUE on every row means an extra dollar sign has locked the row, as in $E$2. Color shifted by one row means the wrong cell was active.'

findings.description: Error 03 claimed that testing rows 2-521 while summing rows 2-500 makes SUMIF answer on the wrong rows silently. Excel actually resizes Sum_range from its top-left cell to the shape of Range, so that case gives the correct answer. The silent failure happens the other way round, when the tested range is the shorter one.
findings.evidence: LibreOffice 24.2 (same documented rule as Excel's SUMIF): =SUMIF(B2:B7,"Norte",E2:E5) -> 1600, identical to the full-range answer. =SUMIF(B2:B4,"Norte",E2:E7) -> 1000, silently missing the 600 on row 5. Microsoft's SUMIF page says the cells added are taken from the top-left of sum_range in the size and shape of range.
findings.fix_summary: Swapped the heights: 'Renglones 2 a 500 probados contra renglones 2 a 521 sumados. Excel los alinea desde arriba y deja fuera los últimos 21 renglones sin decir nada.' (en: 'Rows 2 to 500 tested against rows 2 to 521 added ... leaves the last 21 rows out without a word.') The title and the objective 'Rangos de distinta altura' stay valid.

findings.description: The slide was titled 'Cuatro respuestas malas que no marcan error' / 'Four wrong answers that raise nothing', but Error 02 (a comparison without quotation marks) is not silent: a typed =SUMAR.SI(E2:E521,>500) is refused by Excel's formula parser.
findings.evidence: LibreOffice: =SUMIF(E2:E7;>500) -> Err:510, a parse error. In Excel a typed comparison operator cannot start an argument, so the 'There's a problem with this formula' dialog appears.
findings.fix_summary: Title is now 'Cuatro errores, y tres de ellos no marcan nada' / 'Four mistakes, and three of them raise nothing'. The Error 02 description keeps both original points and adds the real consequence: 'Tecleada sin ellas, Excel rechaza la fórmula; solo un número o una referencia van solos.' / 'Typed bare, Excel refuses the formula; only a number or a reference goes plain.'

findings.description: The 'Línea 6' / 'Line 6' annotation on =PROMEDIO.SI(E2:E521,"<>") claimed the not-blank criterion is what stops empty rows from dragging the average down. AVERAGE and AVERAGEIF already ignore empty cells, so the criterion changes nothing here.
findings.evidence: LibreOffice with E2:E8 = 100, blank, 300, blank, 200, blank, 0: =AVERAGEIF(E2:E8,"<>") -> 150 and =AVERAGE(E2:E8) -> 150, the same result. Only "<>0" changes it (200). Microsoft's AVERAGEIF docs: an empty cell in average_range is ignored. labs/ex09.en.md says the same thing.
findings.fix_summary: es: 'Distinto de nada. Da igual que PROMEDIO: las celdas vacías nunca cuentan como cero.' en: 'Not equal to nothing. Same as AVERAGE here: empty cells never count as zero.'

findings.description: Step 03 ('Todos los rangos a la misma altura') said that ranges not covering the same rows give a silently wrong answer. In SUMIFS, ranges of different heights return #VALUE!; only a range of the same height shifted to other rows fails silently.
findings.evidence: LibreOffice: =SUMIFS(E2:E5,B2:B7,"Norte") -> Err:502 (#VALUE! in Excel, per Microsoft's SUMIFS #VALUE! troubleshooting article). =SUMIFS(E2:E7,B1:B6,"Norte",C2:C7,"marzo") -> 1900 instead of 1400, with no error.
findings.fix_summary: es: 'Los rangos de criterios y el que se suma cubren los mismos renglones. Otra altura da #¡VALOR!; un rango corrido falla en silencio' (quoted because of the #). en: 'The criteria ranges and the sum range cover the same rows. Another height gives #VALUE!; a shifted range is quietly wrong'.

findings.description: The 'Si falla' annotation said a zero where a total belongs almost always means one range starts on the header row. A header-row start actually gives #VALUE! when the range is taller than the others, or a wrong non-zero total when it is the same height. A zero comes from swapped ranges or criteria that do not match.
findings.evidence: LibreOffice: =SUMIFS(E2:E7,B1:B7,"Norte",C2:C7,"marzo") -> Err:502. =SUMIFS(E1:E6,B2:B7,"Norte",C2:C7,"marzo") -> 200. =SUMIFS(E2:E7,B1:B6,...) -> 1900. =SUMIFS(E1:E7,B1:B7,...,C1:C7,...) -> 1400, which is correct. None of these is 0.
findings.fix_summary: Kept the header-row topic and corrected the symptom. es: 'Un rango que empieza en el renglón de los encabezados da #¡VALOR! si queda más alto que los otros, y si mide lo mismo, un total con un renglón de desfase.' en: 'A range that starts on the header row gives #VALUE! if it ends up taller than the others, and if it is the same height, a total one row out.'

findings.description: The panel states as a rule that bars and lines start at zero. Standard visualization guidance requires a zero baseline for bars, because length encodes the value. It does not require one for line charts, which encode by position and slope; forcing zero there can flatten real variation. The lab constraint, 'el eje vertical empieza en cero', applies the same rule even to a scatter plot.
findings.evidence: The same claim appears in the course module's 01_matplotlib_basics.py at line 57 ('a bar or line chart starts at zero, or it lies') and line 101. So it is a deliberate course position, not a slip in this deck.
findings.fix_summary: Not changed. It is the instructor's position, consistent with module A06 and the rubric, so it needs the instructor's decision. A possible wording is 'Las barras empiezan en cero', with a separate note on lines.

findings.description: The panel labeled 'Barras ordenadas' / 'Sorted bars' contains ax.barh(nombres, valores) and no sort. It only shows sorted bars if nombres and valores were sorted beforehand; a plain groupby returns the products in alphabetical order. barh also draws the first item at the bottom, so data sorted descending (as for the pie) puts the largest bar at the bottom.
findings.evidence: Ran both panels on sales_clean.csv. groupby('product') order is Bean subscription, Coffee grinder, Espresso machine, Filter kettle, Travel mug. Pie autopct gives 68%, 13%, 11%, 5%, 3%. The module's 02_chart_types.py sorts explicitly with shares.sort_values() before calling barh.
findings.fix_summary: Not changed. The panel is a two-line illustration that assumes the same pre-sorted data as the pie. Showing the sort would mean rewriting the panel.

findings.description: The note blamed Git Bash's 127 on POSIX shells cutting the status down to eight bits. That is false: the low byte of 0xE0434352 is 0x52 = 82, not 127. The real cause is that Git Bash's MSYS2 runtime replaces Windows exit codes of 0xC0000000 and above with 127 (a few specific ones become signals instead).
findings.evidence: Computed in Python: 0xE0434352 - 2^32 = -532462766, and 0xE0434352 & 0xFF = 82. Fetched msys2-runtime winsup/cygwin/pinfo.cc: set_exit_code does `if (x >= 0xc0000000UL) exitcode = status_exit(x)`, and the default case of status_exit sets `x = 127 << 8`. So 127 is the right measured value, but the stated reason is wrong.
findings.fix_summary: Note now reads '...se reporta como 127, porque su capa POSIX cambia por 127 casi todo código desde 0xC0000000. Por eso el número nunca se cita solo: se nombra el shell junto a él.' It still fits in 3 lines (check.sh CLEAN).

findings.description: Same false claim as the Spanish deck: 'because POSIX shells truncate the status to eight bits'. Truncation would give 82. Git Bash shows 127 because its runtime turns codes of 0xC0000000 and above into 127.
findings.evidence: Same calculation (low byte 0x52 = 82) and the same msys2-runtime pinfo.cc source (x >= 0xc0000000 goes to status_exit, whose default is 127<<8).
findings.fix_summary: Note now reads 'Under Git Bash the same failure reports as 127: its POSIX layer turns almost any code from 0xC0000000 up into 127. So the number is never quoted alone, and the shell is always named beside it.'

findings.description: The model algorithm's abort branch can never run. The MIENTRAS (while) loop only exits once cama >= 60.0, so the next SI cama >= 60.0 test is always true and 'SI NO abortar' (and C#'s else Console.WriteLine(aborto)) is dead code. The note on slide 8 says the right-hand algorithm 'dice qué hacer si no se alcanza', and the Riesgo annotation on slide 14 says what really happens when heating fails: the loop never ends. So the plan does not handle the failure it claims to handle. A student applying the two-person test to this plan will find this.
findings.evidence: Built and ran the slide 15 C# verbatim (.NET 10). The output matches the panel, and after the loop cama is 70.0, so the else branch is unreachable for any start value (cama < 60 loops until >= 60). The same structure is in slide 8 (arranque.txt) and slide 14 (arranque_impresora.txt).
findings.fix_summary: Not fixed: the honest fix is new content, a bounded loop such as 'MIENTRAS cama < 60.0 Y intentos < N' plus a counter. It would touch three code blocks in each language, though the printed output stays the same. Needs the instructor's decision. The alternative is to soften the slide 8 note so it no longer claims the plan handles the not-reached case.

findings.description: Same as the es finding above: 'ELSE abort' / else Console.WriteLine(abort) can never run, because the WHILE only exits at bed >= 60.0. Yet the slide 8 note says the algorithm 'says what to do if it is not reached'.
findings.evidence: Ran the slide 15 en program verbatim: bed ends at 70.0 and the else branch is unreachable for any start value.
findings.fix_summary: Not fixed, for the same reason as es: needs an attempt cap in the loop condition (new content), which is the instructor's call.

findings.description: Slide 14 says the compound operator inserts a cast the long form lacks. The next slide shows `canal += 1` failing with CS0266. Both are true, but neither slide gives the rule that reconciles them, so a reader sees a contradiction. The rule: the implicit cast applies only when the right operand is implicitly convertible to the left type. Constant 100 or 1000 converts to byte or short, but an int constant never converts to char.
findings.evidence: Slide 14: `crc += 100; ventana += 1000;` build succeeded and printed 44 and -32536. The long forms `crc = crc + 100; ventana = ventana + 1000;` give 2 errors, which confirms the title. Slide 15: `canal += 1;` gives CS0266 Cannot implicitly convert type 'int' to 'char'.
findings.fix_summary: No factual error on the slides. Adding the rule would be new content, and the note box is already full. Left for the instructor.

findings.description: The continue row said continue 'salta al tiempo de cambio' / 'jumps to the change beat'. In a while or do-while, continue skips the change beat and goes straight to the condition. Only a for runs its iterator. Slides 21 and 23 of the same deck teach exactly this ('en un while no corre nada'), and the claim is the misconception behind quiz distractor A.
findings.evidence: I ran the quiz program (slide 20). It never ends: timeout exit 124. The capped version (slide 21) prints j = 0 tras 1001 vueltas, so j++ never runs after continue in a while. Microsoft's C# reference says continue 'starts a new iteration of the closest enclosing iteration statement'.
findings.fix_summary: Changed the row to es 'Abandona el resto de la pasada y empieza la siguiente' and en 'Abandons the rest of the pass and starts the next one', which is true for while, do-while and for.

verdicts.finding: es s10 stat: 127 under Git Bash was blamed on 8-bit truncation
verdicts.note: Confirmed. 0xE0434352 & 0xFF = 82, not 127. MSYS2/Cygwin set_exit_code sends any code >= 0xC0000000 to status_exit, whose default case is 127<<8. The auditor's Spanish fix had the right facts but was ambiguous: 'cambia por 127 casi todo código desde 0xC0000000' does not say 'and up'. I reworded it to 'Bajo Git Bash el mismo fallo da 127: su capa POSIX convierte en 127 casi cualquier código de 0xC0000000 en adelante.' A first longer version ran to 4 lines and lint flagged it (9.76" > 9.70"). The final text fits in 3 lines, which I measured with kit.wrap_lines, and check.sh is CLEAN.

findings.description: Error 03 said an unclosed parenthesis is reported on the next line ("Un paréntesis sin cerrar se reclama en la línea siguiente"). That was true before Python 3.10. findings.description: The lead said that if the two inner branches do the same thing, the nesting was really one condition joined with and. That is false. If the inner if and the inner else do the same thing, the inner question is pointless, and the result is 'if A: x else: y', not 'A and B'. A nested if collapses into an and when the inner else and the outer else do the same thing.
findings.evidence: Ran concept_check.py over all four (A, B) cases and compared each shape with 'x if A and B else y'. Equal inner branches: False (not equivalent). Inner else equal to outer else: True (equivalent).
findings.fix_summary: Replaced 'Si las dos ramas internas terminan haciendo lo mismo' with 'Si el else de adentro y el de afuera terminan haciendo lo mismo'. The rest of the lead is unchanged.

findings.description: Error 03 said that reusing i in both loops makes 'the walk fall apart'. In Python a for loop takes its next value from its own iterator, so the outer loop still makes every pass. What goes wrong is any use of i after the inner loop: it holds the inner loop's last value, not the outer row. The Spanish slide made the same claim ('el recorrido se descompone').
findings.evidence: Ran regiones=[3 items], canales=[2 items] with 'for i' in both loops. The outer loop still ran 3 passes and the inner body ran 6 times. After each inner loop, i was 1, so regiones[i] gave 'Centro' every time instead of Norte/Centro/Sur.
findings.fix_summary: EN: 'If both fors use i, the inner one overwrites the outer, and whatever uses i after it reads the wrong row.' ES: 'Si los dos for usan i, el de adentro pisa al de afuera, y lo que use i después de él lee otra fila.'

findings.description: Spanish twin of the finding above: 'el de adentro pisa al de afuera y el recorrido se descompone' is false for Python's for loop. The outer pass count is unaffected; only later uses of i are wrong.
findings.evidence: Same run as the EN finding: the outer loop completed all 3 passes, and i after the inner loop was always 1.
findings.fix_summary: Reworded to 'Si los dos for usan i, el de adentro pisa al de afuera, y lo que use i después de él lee otra fila.'

findings.description: The output panel (AAAA 149 / BBBBAAAA 0 / AAAA 150 0) cannot come from this program. It has two '0' tokens after a 149 and a 150. Each thread prints its numbers in increasing order and prints 0 only once, so no interleaving of the two loops can produce that sequence.

findings.description: The verdict says the no-base-case program 'Compila sin una advertencia'. That is false for the course's compiler and for the others: MSVC raises C4717 (level 1, on by default), GCC 12+ raises -Winfinite-recursion under -Wall, and Clang does the same under -Wall.
findings.evidence: g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra sinbase.cpp gives 'warning: infinite recursion detected [-Winfinite-recursion]'. clang++ -Wall -Wextra gives 'all paths through this function will call itself [-Winfinite-recursion]'. findings.description: Slide 8 says 'Cuenten los new y los delete. Si no dan el mismo número, hay una fuga que encontrar' ('If the numbers differ, there is a leak to find'). As a textual count this is only a heuristic. Releasing on every exit path routinely gives one new and two deletes with no leak. Equal counts also do not rule out a leak: a non-virtual base destructor leaks even with matched counts, and w12 teaches exactly that.
findings.evidence: Wrote /tmp/claude-0/audit/scratch/cpp2-w17/count.cpp: one 'new int[n]' and two 'delete[]', one on an early return. Built it with g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -fsanitize=address. It printed '-1 4' and exit=0, with no LeakSanitizer report. The deck's wording does match w12's teaching ('new y delete van en pareja', 'Cada new tiene su delete').
findings.fix_summary: Not changed. It is the author's deliberate rule of thumb and is consistent with w12. The instructor may want to soften it, for example to 'si no dan el mismo número, revisen cada camino hasta su delete'.

findings.description: The output panel's third line read 'session SessionInitializing'. findings.evidence: I fetched ARSession.cs from AR Foundation 6.0.3 (needle-mirror). OnEnable starts Initialize(); CheckAvailability() sets state = CheckingAvailability and then yields on the ARCore availability promise, which is async (ArPresto_checkApkAvailability callback in ARCoreSessionSubsystem.cs 6.0.3). SessionInitializing is only assigned in Update() (and Reset). I compiled BuildReport.cs verbatim with .NET 10 against minimal UnityEngine/ARFoundation stubs that reproduce that lifecycle order: no warnings. findings.description: 'Contenido hundido / Objetos fuera del XR Origin / Cuélgalos del XR Origin'.
