findings.description: The lead says any node with no incoming control connection never runs. That is false for data-only nodes in Visual Scripting (Get Variable, Add, Vector3 nodes), which have no control ports and are evaluated on demand when a running node pulls their output. Students will meet such nodes in their first graph.
findings.evidence: In Visual Scripting 1.9, only nodes with control input ports wait for a control connection. Value nodes are evaluated lazily from the value port that requests them.
findings.fix_summary: Qualified the sentence: 'Un nodo con puerto de control al que no le entra esa conexión nunca corre...' / 'A node with a control port but no incoming control connection never runs...'. I left the takeaway and the step text unchanged because they are summaries.

findings.description: The annotation says the graph that listens for the event has to live on the target GameObject. The Custom Event node has its own Target input port, which defaults to Self, so a graph on another object can listen to that target.
findings.evidence: In Visual Scripting, CustomEvent is a GameObjectEventUnit whose 'target' value input defaults to the graph's own object (NullMeansSelf). EventBus matches the hook by target GameObject, not by where the graph lives.
findings.fix_summary: '...el grafo que lo escucha vive ahí' -> '...suele vivir ahí'. EN: 'has to be on that object' -> 'usually sits on that object'.

findings.description: The Riesgo annotation says that without RemoveListener 'la escena recargada trae dos'. In the normal single-scene setup, reloading the scene recreates the ARPlaneManager along with its UnityEvent, so you still get one listener. Duplicates come from OnEnable running again on the same manager, for example when the component is disabled and re-enabled.
findings.evidence: Compiled PlaneLog.cs verbatim against Unity API stubs (UnityEvent.AddListener does not dedupe runtime listeners, same as Unity's InvokableCallList). The first OnEnable gives one '+0 ~1' line per event. Calling OnEnable a second time printed '+0 ~1' twice for one event.

The course builds to Android/ARCore, and Google's ARCore docs say ARCore estimates the image's physical width itself; a specified width only makes that faster, and the estimate may differ from it. On ARCore the error may therefore shrink over time instead of staying fixed at 2x.

findings.evidence: The Scripting API contract for hitResults says 'Contents are replaced with the raycast results, if successful', which matches the slide, and the advice 'read only after a true' is correct either way.

findings.description: The built slide shows `if (rp) rp.renderScale = small ? 0.f : 0.f;` while the YAML has `0.7f : 0.9f`. The kit's highlighter silently drops the digit before an f/F suffix in every C# float literal. Students see code with the wrong values.
findings.evidence: python-pptx read of the built es and en .pptx gives runs [' ', '0.', 'f ', ':', ' ', '0.', 'f', ';']. kit.highlight.highlight() on 'float g = 2f;' returns 'float g = f;', on '10.25f' returns '10.f', and on '1.5F' returns '1.F'. Cause: in kit/highlight.py `(?P<num>\b\d+\.?\d*\b)` (line 150 in _TOKEN_RE, used for csharp; the same pattern is at line 142 in _TOKEN_RE_C) backtracks to '0.' because no \b exists between '7' and 'f'. The leftover digit matches no alternative, so finditer skips it. A line-by-line comparison of every code/output line in both decks shows this is the only altered line in this deck.
findings.fix_summary: Not fixable in my YAML without rewriting correct code. Fix in ppts/kit/highlight.py: let the num group take a suffix, e.g. `\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?[fFdDmMuUlL]*\b`, or add a catch-all `(?P<text>.)` alternative so unmatched characters are never dropped. This likely affects every C# deck with float literals (Unity courses).

findings.description: The 'Primero vSyncCount / vSyncCount first' annotation said that with vertical sync on, the target frame rate is ignored, so turn it off first. That is false on Android, the platform this course builds to: mobile platforms ignore QualitySettings.vSyncCount and always use Application.targetFrameRate.
findings.evidence: The Unity Scripting API (Application.targetFrameRate / QualitySettings.vSyncCount) says 'Mobile platforms ignore QualitySettings.vSyncCount. Use Application.targetFrameRate to control the frame rate on mobile platforms' and 'On all other platforms, Unity ignores the value of targetFrameRate if you set vSyncCount' (confirmed by web search of the official pages; docs.unity3d.com itself is blocked here). The Unity manual on profiler markers also says Android and iOS enforce VSync.
findings.fix_summary: ES: 'Fuera del teléfono, con sincronía vertical prendida el objetivo se ignora. Android ignora vSyncCount y respeta el objetivo.' EN: 'Off the phone, with vertical sync on, the target is ignored. Android ignores vSyncCount and honors the target.' The code is unchanged (setting 0 is still right for editor/desktop).

findings.description: The accented 'Riesgo/Risk' annotation said setting targetFrameRate every frame is 'a cost you added'. That property set costs almost nothing, so it is not the real risk. The real risk in every AR scene of this course is that AR Session's Match Frame Rate option rewrites Application.targetFrameRate (and vSyncCount=0) to the camera's rate. Your value from Start then never shows, which defeats the slide title 'Pedir una tasa de frames, y que se note'.
findings.evidence: AR Foundation ARSession API (5.x/6.0) via search: matchFrameRateRequested 'set[s] Application.targetFrameRate to match the native update frequency of the AR session' and sets QualitySettings.vSyncCount to zero. The forum thread 'AR Foundation - Camera Frame Rate defaulting to 30?' shows the effect. AR Session is taught in w02 (GameObject > XR > AR Session), so the term is known.
findings.fix_summary: Risk text replaced, accent and label kept. ES: 'Con Match Frame Rate marcado, AR Session reescribe este valor con la tasa de la cámara.' EN: 'With Match Frame Rate checked, AR Session overwrites this value with the camera's rate.'

findings.description: The question gave 22 ms GPU and 9 ms CPU but no target rate. The deck itself recommends 30 fps (FrameTarget default 30, 'Treinta a propósito'). At 30 fps a 22 ms frame fits in 33.3 ms, so distractor D's conclusion ('Nada') becomes defensible and A is not the only correct answer. The answer slide (21) silently assumes 60 fps ('A 60 fps' column).
findings.evidence: max(9,22)=22 ms < 33.3 ms (30 fps budget) but > 16.7 ms (60 fps budget). The trace on slide 21 compares only against 16.7 ms.
findings.fix_summary: The target is now in the question. ES: 'Con objetivo de 60 fps, el Profiler marca 22 ms de GPU y 9 ms de CPU. ¿Qué recortas primero?' EN: 'Aiming for 60 fps, the Profiler reports 22 ms of GPU and 9 ms of CPU. What do you cut first?' Still 2 lines at full 43.5 pt. A is now the only defensible answer. D stays the 'summed the two and used the wrong budget' confusion that slide 21 rebuts.

findings.description: The 'renderScale' annotation said the passthrough is not affected ('El passthrough no se toca' / 'The passthrough is not affected'). In URP the whole game camera renders into an intermediate color target sized by renderScale. AR Foundation's background renderer feature draws the camera feed into that same target, so the passthrough is downscaled too.
findings.evidence: URP source (Unity-Technologies/Graphics, UniversalRenderPipelineCore.cs via Context7): the camera target descriptor is created with cameraData.scaledWidth/scaledHeight (renderScale applied for game-view cameras). The AR background pass renders into the camera color target before or after opaques.
findings.fix_summary: ES: 'Toda la cámara se dibuja a una fracción de la pantalla y se escala, passthrough incluido.' EN: 'The whole camera renders at a fraction of the screen and is scaled up, passthrough included.'

findings.description: The batching table said GPU Instancing needs only the same mesh and material. In URP (this deck's pipeline, see Quality.cs) the SRP Batcher takes priority, so GPU instancing only happens when the SRP Batcher is off or the shader is made incompatible with it. Checking 'GPU Instancing' on a URP Lit material otherwise does nothing.
findings.evidence: Unity manual, GPU instancing > Render pipeline compatibility: 'In URP or HDRP, GPU instancing requires the SRP Batcher to be disabled or the shader to be made incompatible with it.' SRPBatcher-Incompatible page: 'GPU instancing, which is not compatible with the SRP Batcher'.

findings.description: Both decks said that on Stop the editor 're-reads the scene file from disk' ('vuelve a leer el archivo del disco'). The play-mode concept lead, its step 3, quiz option B, the method statement, the method 'Why it happens' point and the takeaway all repeated it. That is false whenever the scene had unsaved edits before Play. Unity backs up the modified scene when Play starts and restores that pre-Play state on Stop, so unsaved edit-mode changes survive Play and Stop, and the scene file is never re-read.
findings.evidence: Unity manual (Configurable Enter Play Mode): entering Play first backs up the current scenes 'only when the scene is modified', and Stop restores them. Unsaved changes come back after Stop, with the scene still marked dirty. A crash during Play can be recovered from Temp/__Backupscenes/0.backup. Under the slide's model, unsaved changes would be lost on Stop, which does not happen. The quiz key (B) stays correct: a move made during Play is still lost.
findings.fix_summary: Made the same small wording change in all six places in each language: 'reloads the file from disk' became 'restores the scene from before Play' ('regresa la escena de antes del Play'). The rest of the text, including 'que nunca se enteró' / 'which never heard about it', is kept. Option B is still the only correct answer.

findings.description: The accented 'Riesgo'/'Risk' annotation said that after a rename 'the console reads The associated script cannot be loaded, with an empty slot in the Inspector'. That message is a help box on the component in the Inspector, not a Console message, and Unity spells it 'can not'. After a rename made inside Unity the .meta GUID survives, so the Script field is not necessarily empty.
findings.evidence: Unity's generic MonoBehaviour inspector shows the help box 'The associated script can not be loaded. Please fix any compile errors and assign a valid script.' on the component. Renaming the file does not cause a compile error, so nothing reaches the Console from compilation.
findings.fix_summary: es: 'Cambia el nombre del archivo y el componente, en el Inspector, dice The associated script can not be loaded.' en: 'Rename the file and the component in the Inspector reads The associated script can not be loaded.' The accent stays (it is the only one on the slide and the label says Risk).

findings.description: The title 'What changes when the 2D button goes down' ('Qué cambia cuando se activa el botón 2D') attributed every row to the Scene view 2D toggle. The 'In front' row (Sorting Layer, then Order) and the 'Z for sorting' row are properties of 2D sprite rendering. The toggle does not change draw order: sprites sort by Sorting Layer and Order with the button on or off, and opaque meshes still use depth.
findings.evidence: The 2D button only switches the Scene view camera to orthographic, facing the XY plane, with rotation locked. Renderer sorting (Sorting Layer, Order in Layer, then camera distance under the default transparency sort mode) does not depend on it. Rows 1 and 2 are about the button; rows 3 and 4 are about working with sprites.
findings.fix_summary: Retitled to 'Qué cambia cuando trabajas en 2D' / 'What changes when you work in 2D', which is true for all four rows. The eyebrow 'El botón 2D' and the agenda card are unchanged and still describe rows 1 and 2.

findings.description: 'el clon vive hasta que el objeto se destruye' / 'the clone lives until the object is destroyed' is false. Unity does not free a material instantiated by Renderer.material when the GameObject is destroyed. The Renderer.material reference says destroying it is your responsibility. Otherwise it is freed only by Destroy or Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets, for example on a scene load.
findings.evidence: Context7 Unity manual (performance-managed-memory-introduction): native memory is cleared only when Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets is called or Destroy is called on the object. findings.description: steps = (int)(t / Time.fixedDeltaTime) truncates. The panel shows 32 only if Time.time at contact is exactly 32*0.02f. If the time base accumulated in float, t = 0.6399999 and the cast gives 31. Unity keeps time in double internally (fixedTimeAsDouble), so 32 is what Unity should print, but the code is fragile. Math.RoundToInt would be robust.
findings.evidence: Compiled the verbatim es and en fragments with a UnityEngine stub (.NET 10, no warnings). Simulated semi-implicit Euler with g=9.81 and dt=0.02: first penetration at step 32 (theory 0.6386 s = 31.93 steps). Time accumulated in double: output 'altura de caída 2.00 m / primer contacto 0.64 s / pasos fijos 32' (en same), which matches the panel. Float accumulation: t=0.6399999, steps=31.
findings.fix_summary: Not changed: the panel matches what Unity's double time base produces. Reported as a robustness caveat.

A DROP PROCEDURE without IF EXISTS fails on the FIRST run on a fresh database, with 1305, and in batch mode it keeps failing on every run. With no DROP line at all, the second run dies with 1304 (already exists), not 1305. The same error is in the English deck.
findings.evidence: Ran it on MariaDB 10.11, which uses the same legacy codes as MySQL. Script without the DROP line, second run: 'ERROR 1304 (42000): PROCEDURE sp_creditos already exists'. Script with 'DROP PROCEDURE sp_creditos' on a fresh database: 'ERROR 1305 (42000) at line 1: PROCEDURE ... does not exist' on the first run, and again on the second run because the CREATE never executed.
findings.fix_summary: es: 'Sin el DROP, la segunda corrida del script muere con ERROR 1304 (42000) y ...'; en: 'Without the DROP the second run of the script dies with ERROR 1304 (42000), ...'

findings.description: The objectives and the table title say 'un solo 23000 para toda la integridad' / 'a single 23000 for the whole of integrity'. In MySQL a CHECK constraint violation is ERROR 3819 (HY000), not 23000. Week 6 of this course shows 3819 (HY000) on screen, and w14 contrasts 1644 with 3819. Only keys (duplicate, FK) and NOT NULL give 23000. Same in en.
findings.evidence: Grep: w06.es s~13 output shows 'ERROR 3819 (HY000): Check constraint ... is violated' under MySQL 9.7.2. Ran the table cases on MariaDB: 1365/22012, 1264/22003, 1406/22001, 1062/23000, 1452/23000 and 1048/23000 all match the table. MariaDB's CHECK gives 4025 (23000), a dialect difference; MySQL gives 3819 (HY000).
findings.fix_summary: '... y un solo 23000 para llaves y NOT NULL' (es) / '... a single 23000 for keys and NOT NULL' (en), in objectives and table title of both decks

findings.description: The table row 'Subconsulta | no, si es correlacionada' (en: 'A subquery | no, if correlated') turns one measured case into a rule for every subquery. The case on slide 13 (escalar.sql, v_escalar) is a scalar subquery in the select list. MySQL's documented rules for subqueries in WHERE are different: a correlated EXISTS on another table stays updatable, and a subquery on the view's own table blocks updates even when it is not correlated.
findings.evidence: Compared against the MySQL 8.0/8.4 reference 'Updatable and Insertable Views'. A subquery in the select list blocks INSERT, and a dependent one blocks every data change. A subquery in WHERE that refers to a table in the FROM clause is a separate rule. The companion solutions file (soluciones.es.md 12.1) calls the measured case 'subconsulta escalar'. My first fix, 'Subconsulta escalar' in the label cell, wrapped: check.sh reported 'rows end at 10.09", footer rule at 9.76"', so I moved the qualifier into the second cell.
findings.fix_summary: es: second cell now reads 'no, si es escalar y correlacionada'. en: 'no, if scalar and correlated'. check.sh is CLEAN.

findings.evidence: Same reasoning as slide 14: slide 13 measured only a select-list scalar subquery, and a correlated EXISTS in WHERE is mergeable and updatable in MySQL.
findings.fix_summary: Changed to 'Con una subconsulta escalar correlacionada…' and 'With a correlated scalar subquery…'. Both still fit (CLEAN).

findings.description: The Restricción block requires the coordinator view to come from week 11's JOIN and rules out a single-table view. That spoils the experiment. A newly inserted alumno has no inscripciones, so he vanishes from an INNER JOIN view whatever his carrera. The 'lost row' therefore comes from the JOIN, not from the carrera filter that WITH CHECK OPTION is meant to guard. Two more mismatches: the companion exercise 12.2 (ejercicios.es.md / soluciones.es.md) builds the coordinator view from a single table (FROM equipo WHERE linea_id = 1), and the 'La prueba' block asks for an UPDATE that the brief never mentions.

Without the clause, an INSERT of another carrera and an INSERT of the same carrera both returned 0 rows in the view. With WITH CHECK OPTION, both INSERTs failed with ERROR 1369, including the same-carrera one. MySQL may evaluate only the WHERE, but the confound is still there. With a single-table view, the documented result is 0 in the view and 1 in the table.

findings.description: The title says the unguarded validation 'is a validation that does not validate', and the note implies the IS NOT NULL guard on the right changes the outcome. In fact `IF x IS NOT NULL AND (x<0 OR x>10)` and `IF x<0 OR x>10` behave the same for every input. NULL makes the left condition unknown and the right one false, and IF skips both, so the NULL row gets in either way. The course's own exercise 14.2 ("deja pasar el vacío") and its solution say the guarded trigger lets NULL in on purpose.
findings.evidence: MariaDB 10.11. With the guarded trigger, INSERT with calificacion NULL went in. After swapping in the unguarded trigger, a second NULL row also went in, while 11.0 and -1 were rejected with 1644. Truth table for v in NULL,-1,0,5,10,11 gave sin_guarda NULL,1,0,0,0,1 and con_guarda 0,1,0,0,0,1: the IF enters only for -1 and 11 in both.
findings.fix_summary: New title: 'El NULL pasa por las dos, y solo una lo dice' / 'NULL gets through both, and only one of them says so'. The last sentence of the note now says the guard does not change the result; it makes it a written decision instead of an accident.

Calling one with SELECT gave ERROR 1415 (0A000) Not allowed to return a result set from a trigger. Calling one with an EXIT HANDLER ... ROLLBACK gave ERROR 1422 (HY000) Explicit or implicit commit is not allowed in stored function or trigger.

findings.description: Both INSERTs use VALUES with 4 values and no column list. Inside the same deck, slide 8 shows inscripciones with matricula, clave_materia, periodo and calificacion, and slide 12 updates by inscripcion_id, so the table has at least 5 columns and these INSERTs fail with 1136 before the trigger ever runs.
findings.evidence: MariaDB: on a 5-column table, the original INSERT gave ERROR 1136 (21S01) Column count doesn't match value count. The edited slide code, run verbatim on both 4-column and 5-column tables with 6 seed rows, gives counts 6, then 7, then ERROR 1644 (45000) La calificacion debe estar entre 0 y 10, then still 7, then 6 after ROLLBACK. That matches the slide's output panel exactly.

findings.description: Error 04 says 'SHOW TRIGGERS guarda el Definer y el sql_mode' / 'SHOW TRIGGERS keeps...'. SHOW TRIGGERS only displays them. The server stores them with the trigger at creation time.
findings.evidence: information_schema.TRIGGERS and SHOW TRIGGERS expose SQL_MODE and DEFINER captured at CREATE time. Checked in MariaDB. The other three pitfall codes are real: 1363 at creation for OLD in an INSERT trigger (and NEW in a DELETE trigger), 1442 at runtime for UPDATE of the same table, and 1360 for DROP TRIGGER on a missing trigger, which IF EXISTS turns into Note 1360.
findings.fix_summary: 'guarda' changed to 'muestra' and 'keeps' to 'shows'.

findings.description: 'la derecha sola ... possible_keys=NULL' is probably wrong on 9.7.2. Since MySQL 8.0.13, skip-scan key collection adds an index that covers the query to possible_keys even when the optimizer then rejects the skip scan for cost. The full index scan would then show possible_keys=idx_mat_fecha. Applies to en as well.
findings.evidence: The course's own 9.7.2 run in soluciones.es.md 15.1, same query shape (WHERE second column only, covering composite index), shows 'index idx_eq_fecha idx_eq_fecha ... 199963'. possible_keys is filled there. The MySQL 8.0 manual's skip-scan example lists possible_keys: PRIMARY for a predicate on the second key part. MariaDB 10.11, which has no skip scan, gives possible_keys NULL, which is the slide's value, so the slide may come from a non-skip-scan server.
findings.fix_summary: Not fixed because it cannot be executed on 9.7.2 here. Recommend re-running EXPLAIN FORMAT=TRADITIONAL on 9.7.2 and correcting possible_keys in both decks. The lesson still holds through type=index and rows≈table size.

findings.description: The retry code does not retry, and it cannot produce the output shown. The CONTINUE handler only increments v_intentos inside the handler. After it runs, execution falls through to an unconditional COMMIT and LEAVE, so the failed work is lost and the loop never runs a second time. v_intentos counts failures, not attempts (A would show 0, not 1). The code updates only row 1, so it cannot deadlock with itself, yet the output shows rows 1 and 2.
findings.evidence: I ran it on MariaDB 10.11 as a procedure called from two sessions with the row order reversed (two UPDATEs so a 1213 can happen). Slide code: A intentos 0, B intentos 1, and each row only +100 because B's work was lost. Corrected code (flag set in the handler, attempt counter at the top of the loop, IF v_falla = 0 THEN COMMIT; LEAVE; END IF, rows p_primera/p_segunda as in exercise 16.3): A intentos 1 / quedo_fallando 0, B intentos 2 / quedo_fallando 0. Starting from 15400/12400, the rows end at 15600.00/12600.00, which matches the panel exactly.
findings.fix_summary: Rewrote the 14-line fragment as a real retry loop. Added DECLARE v_falla, the handler does ROLLBACK and sets v_falla = 1, the loop resets the flag and counts attempts, two UPDATEs on p_primera/p_segunda, and the COMMIT/LEAVE is conditional. The output is unchanged.

findings.description: Same broken retry loop as the Spanish deck. There is an unconditional COMMIT and LEAVE after a CONTINUE handler, the handler counts failures instead of attempts, and the code touches one row while the output shows two.

findings.fix_summary: Same corrected fragment as es, so code behavior is at parity.

findings.description: Neither case opens a transaction. With the default autocommit=1, the first UPDATE (+500 on row 3) commits on its own, so the later 1213 cannot undo it. The panel's 'fila 3 9000.00 ... volvió a su valor' therefore contradicts the code shown, and so does the title's claim that the whole transaction is undone. The deck's own pitfall 01 and w08 teach exactly this autocommit trap.
findings.evidence: MariaDB: without START TRANSACTION, row 3 ends at 9500.00 after B's 1213. With START TRANSACTION, it ends at 9000.00 after 1213 + COMMIT. Case 2 with START TRANSACTION: the 1205 leaves @@in_transaction = 1 and the COMMIT persists 7777.00, which matches the panel.
findings.fix_summary: Added 'START TRANSACTION;' at the top of case 1 and case 2 (13 lines, still at least 18 pt, check CLEAN).

findings.description: Error 03 says the three cases (DDL, LOCK TABLES, MyISAM) lose 'todas o ninguna' 'sin un solo aviso'. A ROLLBACK after changing a MyISAM table inside a transaction does raise a warning: 1196 ER_WARNING_NOT_COMPLETE_ROLLBACK, documented for MySQL too. None of the three raises an error.
findings.evidence: MariaDB: START TRANSACTION; INSERT into a MyISAM table; ROLLBACK gives 'Query OK, 0 rows affected, 1 warning', and SHOW WARNINGS shows 'Warning 1196 Some non-transactional changed tables couldn't be rolled back'. LOCK TABLES and DDL implicit commits produced no warning.

findings.description: 'Una lectura simple nunca espera' is stated without a qualifier. It holds only below SERIALIZABLE. Under SERIALIZABLE inside a transaction, a plain SELECT becomes a locking read (FOR SHARE) and can wait. The deck's own pitfall 04 relies on SERIALIZABLE reads taking locks.
findings.evidence: MariaDB: a SERIALIZABLE session that only read row 1 inside a transaction made a REPEATABLE READ session's UPDATE fail with 1205 after 3 s, so its plain read held a shared lock. At REPEATABLE READ the plain read returned at once.
findings.fix_summary: Prefixed 'En el nivel de fábrica,' (the deck's own phrase from pitfall 04).

findings.description: Same unqualified 'A plain read never waits'.

unverifiable: Slides 11 and 12: the performance_schema.data_locks listings (PRIMARY 1..5 plus the supremum pseudo-record; X / X,GAP / X,REC_NOT_GAP on idx_alumno_carrera) are MySQL 8+ only. MariaDB 10.11 has no data_locks. The blocking behavior they imply was reproduced: without the index, B's UPDATE of row 5 and B's INSERT both got 1205; with the index, the UPDATE passed and the INSERT got 1205 on the gap. The listings match InnoDB REPEATABLE READ next-key semantics by reading.

Slide 10: FOR SHARE syntax and the NOWAIT error 3572 (ER_LOCK_NOWAIT) are MySQL-specific. MariaDB rejects FOR SHARE and returns 1205 for NOWAIT. I checked them against MySQL 8+ documentation semantics.

Slide 18: the MySQL client wording 'Lost connection to MySQL server during query' and the STATE 'updating'. MariaDB prints 'Lost connection to server during query' and 'Updating'. The error code 2013 and the pid semantics were verified.
Slide 7: lock_wait_timeout factory value 31536000 s is MySQL's default (MariaDB's is 86400). The other five defaults were confirmed on the server and match MySQL.

Slide 19: the absolute values 15600.00 / 12600.00 depend on a starting state the deck never shows. They were reproduced from 15400/12400 with the corrected code; the +200 per row and intentos 1/2 are what was verified.

Pitfall 02: the trigger's COUNT(*) is a consistent (non-waiting) read in MySQL only with binlog off or binlog_format=ROW (the MySQL 8+ default). It was verified on MariaDB with binlog off: the trigger saw 0 at once, and the UNIQUE index waited 4.9 s and returned 1062.
Lab (slide 21) and covers: that 'MySQL 9.7.2' exists as a release could not be checked offline. It is used consistently across the whole course.
Neither deck has speaker notes (no 'notes' key in any MySQL week), so there were no notes to audit.

findings.evidence: Shell semantics. Ran the operador scenario on the private MariaDB (SELECT, LOCK TABLES, SHOW VIEW, EVENT, TRIGGER on db_backup.*, mysqldump --routines): exit=0, grep -c PROCEDURE = 0, so the procedure is left out silently. MariaDB does not dump tablespaces, so its stderr was empty. The MySQL 8.0.21+ PROCESS tablespace message cannot be reproduced here.

findings.description: Trap 04 said SOURCE "dentro de un script contesta ERROR 1064, porque el servidor nunca la recibe" (EN: "inside a script it answers ERROR 1064, because the server never receives it"). This contradicts itself: 1064 is a server parse error, so it happens exactly when the server does receive SOURCE. A script fed to the mysql client runs SOURCE fine.
findings.evidence: Private MariaDB: `mariadb < outer.sql`, where outer.sql contains `SOURCE inner.sql`, ran inner.sql (exit 0). `PREPARE s FROM 'SOURCE /tmp/x.sql'`, which makes the server parse it, gave ERROR 1064 (42000).
findings.fix_summary: ES: "y fuera del cliente mysql contesta ERROR 1064, porque el servidor no la conoce". EN: "and outside the mysql client it answers ERROR 1064, because the server does not know it". The title and the last sentence are kept.

unverifiable: VBA cannot run in real Excel here. All 12 code/code_output/trace/quiz snippets (6 per language) plus the pitfall expressions were run in LibreOffice 24.2 Basic with Option VBASupport 1, a dialect. The structural results (cell writes, the Offset targets, the ActiveCell trace $C$1,$C$1,$C$3,$C$3, Overflow error 6, Long holding 1,048,576, Dim a, b leaving a as a Variant) agree with the slides.

LibreOffice differs from VBA on three points the slides claim: it rounds 2.5 to 3 (VBA banker's rounding gives 2), it evaluates "5a" + 3 to 8 (VBA raises error 13), and it assigns 0 for text into a Long (VBA raises error 13). For these the slides were checked against Microsoft's documented semantics and the course HANDOFF.md table of Excel 16.0 results, which match the slides.

The Option Explicit compile error ('Variable not defined', with the editor pointing at the line) cannot be reproduced headless. LibreOffice simply did not run the Sub. The slide's claim 'Ya no compila' / 'It stops compiling' matches the Microsoft reference.

findings.description: The Riesgo/Risk annotation said that if you later add Format's result ('sumas eso'), VBA concatenates it. That holds only when both operands are text. A Format string plus a number is not concatenated: in VBA '0.95%' is not numeric, so it stops with error 13.

MsgBox/CStr display '9.48879293458305E-03' (slide 12): LibreOffice prints 0.00948879293458305. The E-03 form follows VBA's 15-digit conversion and is recorded in HANDOFF's Excel run. The number itself is confirmed: 0.009488792934583046.

'0.95%' + 1 is a Type mismatch (error 13) in real VBA: LibreOffice Basic returned 1.95 instead. Either way the result is not concatenation, which is what the fix relies on.

Excel object model on slides 16 and 17 (Names.Add, Range(name).Address/.Value/.Cells.Count, Names(...).RefersTo, silent redefinition by a second Names.Add): checked against Microsoft documentation semantics and HANDOFF, not executed.

Slide 13: Range("B2").Value = Format(...) most likely makes Excel parse the string '0.95%' back into the number 0.0095, so B2 holds a number, not text. The slide does not claim otherwise, but this cannot be confirmed without Excel.

findings.description: The accent 'Riesgo' annotation said that if column 1 has gaps, End(xlUp) stops at the first gap from the bottom and the range comes out short. That is false. Starting from row 1,048,576, End(xlUp) skips every empty cell and stops at the last value, so gaps in the middle do not matter. It comes out short only when column 1 ends before the column being formatted. The claim also contradicts slide 17 Error 03, which correctly says xlUp from the bottom does not have the gap problem.
findings.evidence: Ran the slide's code verbatim in LibreOffice 24.2 Calc in VBA mode (Option VBASupport 1, via UNO) on a header plus 40 data rows. With A5 and A20 empty, End(xlUp).Row returned 41 and C41 was formatted. With A40:A41 empty, End(xlUp).Row returned 39, and C40 and C41 stayed General.
findings.fix_summary: Changed to 'Si la columna 1 acaba antes que la 3, End(xlUp) se detiene en su último dato y el rango sale corto.' ('la 3' instead of 'las otras' to stay inside the margin).

findings.description: The IsNumeric table sits under the Worksheet_Change code. Its columns are 'Lo que se escribe' / 'What gets typed' and 'Qué escribe al lado' / 'What it writes beside it', so it describes typing into the cell. It listed $5 and 5% as False / 'No es número'. Excel parses the entry before the handler runs: $5 becomes 5 with currency format and 5% becomes 0.05, so IsNumeric(Target.Value) is True and the macro writes 'Número'. Even as a plain string, IsNumeric("$5") is True under Mexico regional settings, because $ is the local currency symbol.
findings.evidence: In LibreOffice Calc 24.2, setFormula (equivalent to typing) turned '$5' into the number 5, '5%' into 0.05, '2026-01-01' into a date and 'abc' into text. In LibreOffice Basic with VBASupport, IsNumeric is True on a Currency and on 0.05, and False on a Date variant. The instructor's own grading note in soluciones.es.md week 11 says: 'Medido con Excel 16.0 en región de México, escribir esos tres valores en una celda deja Target.Value en 5 ... numéricos'. Exercise 11.1(c) is built on exactly this difference. The Microsoft VBA reference says IsNumeric returns False for a date expression, so the 2026-01-01 row (False) was kept.

findings.description: The Riesgo annotation said that a private field named the same as the property makes VBA recurse until the stack runs out. findings.description: The Risk annotation said the second run of CrearTabla/CreateTable fails 'because the name already exists'. In fact the second run fails earlier, at ListObjects.Add, because A1.CurrentRegion is already a table and a new table cannot overlap an existing one (error 1004). The tbl.Name line is never reached.
findings.evidence: Excel raises run-time error 1004 'A table cannot overlap a range that contains a PivotTable report, query results, protected cells or another table' when ListObjects.Add gets a range that intersects an existing ListObject. A web search turned up several forum threads with this exact message for ListObjects.Add. On the second run the source range is the table itself.
findings.fix_summary: es: '...la segunda truena porque ese rango ya es una tabla.' en: '...the second one fails, because that range is already a table.'

findings.description: The RemoveSubtotal annotation said that without it 'la segunda corrida corta sobre los cortes / the second run breaks over the breaks'. Range.Subtotal's Replace argument defaults to True, so Subtotal alone does not stack new subtotals on old ones. In this macro, what goes wrong without RemoveSubtotal is that the Sort runs over a CurrentRegion that still holds the old total rows and moves them into the data.
findings.evidence: From MicrosoftDocs/VBA-Docs api/Excel.Range.Subtotal.md: 'Replace ... True to replace existing subtotals. The default value is True.' I traced the second run by hand: CurrentRegion includes 'Compras Total' and 'Grand Total' ('Total general' in a Spanish UI), and sorting A ascending moves the grand total row up between the departments.
findings.fix_summary: es: 'Primero limpia los cortes anteriores. Si no, el Sort revuelve las filas de total con los datos.' en: 'Clear the previous breaks first, or the Sort shuffles the old total rows into the data.'

findings.description: Slide 21 says Tables.bas does not compile and 'no corre ni la primera instrucción'. findings.evidence: The Tables.bas source has 'Dim found As Boolean' at lines 144 and 197 of AddColumnToTable, so the module does not compile. The trace on slide 23 assumes the MsgBox line runs.
findings.fix_summary: es stem: 'Sin Option Explicit y ya sin el Dim repetido, ¿qué muestra el mensaje?' en stem: 'No Option Explicit, and the repeated Dim is gone. What does the message show?' Option A is now the only defensible answer: B is a misconception, C needs Option Explicit, and D needs an object variable.

findings.description: The panel says WorksheetFunction.Left(...) gives 'Error 438 Object doesn't support this property or method'. WorksheetFunction is an early-bound, non-extensible type, so a missing member is caught when the code compiles. The result is 'Compile error: Method or data member not found' (error 461), and the macro never starts. Runtime 438 is what late-bound calls such as Application.Foo give. The same defect is in the en deck.
findings.evidence: I could not run VBA here, and the network proxy blocked forum and learn.microsoft.com pages. Web search snippets agree that WorksheetFunction.Left fails with 'Method or data member not found' because Left is not a WorksheetFunction member. This matches Excel's typelib behavior: compile-time member check on WorksheetFunction, late binding only on Application.
findings.fix_summary: Output replaced with 'Compile error: / Method or data member / not found' in es and en.

findings.description: The title 'Las tres formas de pedir la misma función' does not describe the slide. The three calls are WorksheetFunction.Left, Left and WorksheetFunction.Trim, so they use two different functions. The en title 'The same function asked for three ways' has the same problem.
findings.evidence: Source lines 1, 3 and 5 of the slide: Left, Left, Trim.
findings.fix_summary: Title changed to 'Tres llamadas y lo que contesta cada una' / 'Three calls and what each one gives back'.

findings.description: The panel showed '[a b]' for WorksheetFunction.Trim("a    b"). The returned value is 'a b', and the brackets are not part of it (the Left result is not bracketed either). Same in en.
findings.evidence: Excel TRIM collapses runs of inner spaces and strips the ends. A Python model of the same rule gives 'a b'.
findings.fix_summary: Brackets removed. The output now shows 'a b' in es and en.

findings.description: The lead says 'Left, Mid y Replace son de VBA y no aparecen en WorksheetFunction'. That is false for Replace: WorksheetFunction.Replace exists. It is Excel's position-based REPLACE(old, start, n, new), which behaves differently from VBA's Replace. Same claim in en.
findings.evidence: Microsoft Learn documents 'WorksheetFunction.Replace method (Excel)', syntax expression.Replace(Arg1, Arg2, Arg3, Arg4), and I confirmed it by web search. Len, Left and Mid have no WorksheetFunction member.
findings.fix_summary: Replace swapped for Len in es and en ('Left, Mid y Len' / 'Left, Mid and Len').

findings.description: The es lead named 'SumarSi', which is not a real Excel function name (SUMAR.SI, without the dot). The en lead names SumIfs (SUMAR.SI.CONJUNTO), so the two decks named different functions. Elsewhere the deck teaches SumIfs (slide 13 and the lab).
findings.evidence: es: 'BuscarV, SumarSi y Contar.Si'. en: 'VLookup, SumIfs and CountIf'. In Spanish Excel, SUMIFS is SUMAR.SI.CONJUNTO.
findings.fix_summary: es now reads 'BuscarV, Sumar.Si.Conjunto y Contar.Si', which matches en and the SumIfs the deck uses.

findings.description: The SERIES formula in the panel references 'Sheet1!', but slide 19's macro builds the chart from ThisWorkbook.Sheets("Datos") (en: "Data"). The real formula would reference Datos!/Data!. The panel also added a space before the last argument (', 1)'), which Excel does not write.
findings.evidence: Slide 19: Set ws = ThisWorkbook.Sheets("Datos"); ch.Chart.SetSourceData ws.Range("A1:B3"). Excel writes =SERIES(Datos!$B$1,Datos!$A$2:$A$3,Datos!$B$2:$B$3,1) with no spaces. Same defect in en with 'Data'.
findings.fix_summary: Sheet1 changed to Datos (es) / Data (en), and ', 1)' changed to ',1)'. The wrap across lines is kept for space.

findings.description: Under the header 'En A1 sería' (en 'In A1 it would be'), the RC row said 'Se usa poco, casi nunca' / 'Rarely used at all'. findings.evidence: Microsoft Learn, Err.Source: 'For errors in a standard module, Source contains the project name.' I ran the handler with stub Limpiar/Ordenar/Reportar in LibreOffice 24.2 Basic (Option VBASupport 1), with Ordenar dividing by zero. The error from the called sub reached Falla, and Source carried no procedure name (empty in LO, 'VBAProject' in Excel). After the edit the run printed 'Se detuvo con el error 11: Division by zero.'

findings.description: Possible problem, not verified. Slide 18's Workbook_Open protects every worksheet with UserInterfaceOnly. The lab then asks that adding rows and rerunning puts them in the summary. Excel is widely reported not to extend UserInterfaceOnly to PivotTable creation or refresh, nor to growing a ListObject, on a protected sheet. If so, the lab criterion fails with 1004 unless the Resumen and Datos sheets are excluded or unprotected around the refresh. The English deck has the same text.
findings.evidence: This could not be run: there is no Excel here, and LibreOffice does not enforce sheet protection against macros (my LO run wrote A1 even without UserInterfaceOnly). The Microsoft Learn Worksheet.Protect page does not list these exceptions. The claim rests on recurring reports from practitioners. It needs a 5-minute test in Excel 365 before class. A fix would go in the lab constraint text of both decks.
findings.fix_summary: Not changed: unverified, and a fix would mean writing new lab content. Flagged for the instructor.

unverifiable: Excel VBA cannot run here. I ran slides 10, 11, 13 (original and edited handler), 16, 17 and quiz 19 / trace 20 in LibreOffice 24.2 Basic with Option VBASupport 1 as a stand-in. Results: CDbl("no soy número") gives Err 13 Type mismatch; Err stays 11 across x = 2 + 2; Err.Clear gives 0; an error in a called sub reaches the caller's handler; a missing Exit Sub runs the handler with Err 0; and in the quiz, Err stays set through total = 2 + 2, so the message shows. LibreOffice is not faithful in two places: a Variant 1 / 0 raises no error (Excel VBA raises error 11, as the course HANDOFF records from a real Excel run), and Workbooks.Open on a missing file gives LO error 1 instead of Excel's 1004.

verdicts.note: Read both .bas files in docs/en/courses/vba-course/09: both declare SubFunctions, SetupFieldsInWorksheet, ReadInputParameters and ReadInputParametersValidation, and Summation is only in SubsFunctions.bas. VBA looks in the calling module first, so the Calls inside SubFunctions are not ambiguous. Only a call from another module gets 'Ambiguous name detected'. verdicts.finding: 16 code_output: cell output copied the MsgBox string 9.48879293458305E-03 / 0.113865515214997
verdicts.note: Recomputed: 0.009488792934583046 and 0.11386551521499655. Excel's General format shows at most 11 characters, which gives 0.009488793 and 0.113865515 (LibreOffice Format('0.000000000') gives the same). Excel never puts the 15-digit VBA string form in a cell. A default-width column would show fewer digits, but 11 characters is General's maximum, so the fix is defensible.

findings.description: Error 03 says 'p.dibujar imprime la referencia al método'. In a .py script, which is what the lab produces, a bare p.dibujar prints nothing and silently does nothing. Only the interactive REPL echoes the reference. The same defect is in en ('p.draw prints the method reference').
findings.evidence: Ran a script containing the bare statement p.dibujar followed by print('fin'). The output was only 'fin'. print(p.dibujar) printed '<bound method Punto.dibujar of ...>'.
findings.fix_summary: es: 'p.dibujar es solo la referencia al método. p.dibujar() lo ejecuta.' en: 'p.draw is only the method reference. p.draw() runs it.'

findings.description: Error 02 says a class-body attribute makes every object share 'la misma lista o el mismo contador'. A counter in the class body incremented through self is not shared, because self.contador += 1 creates an instance attribute. w04's quiz and trace ('Imprime 0') teach exactly this, so the claim contradicts the next session. The same defect is in en ('or the same counter').
findings.evidence: Ran: class C: contador = 0; __init__ does self.contador += 1; then a = C(); b = C(). Result: a.contador=1, b.contador=1, C.contador=0. w04.es slide quiz contador.py says the same.
findings.fix_summary: Dropped 'o el mismo contador' / 'or the same counter'. The list case is the one that is really shared.

findings.description: Distractor D, '2, porque cada carrito duplica la lista', does not follow from the confusion it states. If each cart duplicated the list, b's list would be empty and the answer would be 0, not 2. The same defect is in en ('2, because each cart copies the list'). The deck has no speaker notes, so the answer key is the trace slide 'Imprime 1'.
findings.evidence: Ran compartido.py and shared.py: both print 1, so the key (B) is correct. With per-object lists (the compare 'after' code) len(b.productos) is 0. Nothing produces 2 through duplication.
findings.fix_summary: D now reads '2, porque se crearon dos carritos' / '2, because two carts were created'. This is a coherent confusion (counting objects instead of items) and matches the style of w04's quiz distractor.

findings.description: The lead says the class 'no ocupa memoria por sí misma'. In Python a class is an object of type type: it lives in memory and holds the methods and the class attributes. The deck itself later shows the list 'vive en la clase' (slides 16 to 18). The same defect is in en ('it costs no memory by itself').
findings.evidence: Ran: type(Punto) is <class 'type'>, sys.getsizeof(Punto) is 1688, and 'dibujar' in vars(Punto) is True.
findings.fix_summary: es: 'La clase se escribe una sola vez y existe una sola vez en memoria. Cada objeto que sale de ella ocupa la suya, con su propia copia de los datos.' en: 'You write the class once and it exists once in memory. Every object made from it takes up its own memory, and carries its own copy of the data.'

findings.description: The Clase block says 'No guarda valores', but slides 17 and 18 show the class holding ['X1'] for every cart, and w04 teaches class members (especie, censo). The same defect is in en ('Stores no values of its own').
findings.evidence: Trace slide 17: the Carrito.productos column holds ['X1']. Figure class-vs-instance.png shows the class body holding ['X1'].
findings.fix_summary: es: 'No guarda los datos de cada objeto.' en: 'Holds none of each object's data.'

findings.description: The pull quote credited to Alan Kay is partly a paraphrase. Only 'The big idea is messaging' is his. 'The focus should be on how objects communicate, not on how they are built inside' is not his wording. His 1998 Squeak-list message says the key is to design how the modules communicate rather than their internal properties and behaviors.
findings.evidence: The text of Kay's Oct 1998 squeak-dev message ('prototypes vs classes') is from memory. I could not fetch it: wiki.c2.com and lists.squeakfoundation.org are blocked by the egress proxy.
findings.fix_summary: English is now Kay's two sentences joined by an ellipsis: 'The big idea is messaging… The key in making great and growable systems is much more to design how its modules communicate rather than what its internal properties and behaviors should be.' Spanish is a faithful translation. The source line is unchanged. Both fit (check CLEAN, rendered and inspected).

findings.description: Both setter examples (es and en) use raise ValueError(...), but the deck never explains raise. findings.description: Distractor C '6, porque c vale cero cuando no se pasa' does not follow from the confusion it states. If c defaulted to zero, the call would give 1+2+0 = 3, not 6. The same defect is in the en deck ('6, because c is zero when it is not passed').
findings.evidence: Ran the quiz source (quiz_es.py / quiz_en.py) with python3. The real result is 'TypeError: Calculadora.sumar() missing 1 required positional argument: 'c'', so B is the only correct option and slide 8 (compare) says the same. findings.description: The row 'Tipos distintos' offers functools.singledispatch for a method (every other row shows def ...(self, ...)). findings.evidence: sd.py: a class method decorated with @singledispatch plus an int registration returned 'generico' for crear(5). The same class with @singledispatchmethod returned 'int' for 5 and 'generico' for 'x'.

findings.description: Error 03 says that if carrito imports cliente and cliente imports carrito, 'Python falla a media carga con ImportError' (en: 'Python fails mid-load with ImportError'). Only 'from x import Name' at module level raises ImportError, and module-level attribute use raises AttributeError.
findings.evidence: circ1 (mutual 'import cliente' / 'import carrito', used inside methods) ran OK. circ2 (mutual 'from ... import ...') raised ImportError: cannot import name 'Carrito' from partially initialized module. circ3 (attribute used at load) raised AttributeError: partially initialized module.
